title: Hebrides
body_text: Nequam’s Voyage North The Maelstrom’s Maw sailed north along the English coast, bound for the Hebrides. The elementalist magus Nequam remained cloistered in his tarp-covered shipboard lab, barely emerging except to bark orders at the captain or issue magical instructions. Unlike Dustin's carefully orchestrated trade routes, Nequam left the provisioning and navigation to the crew. The journey became one of incidental trade and self-directed exploration, a loose course charted more by whim and weather than design. Two grogs accompanied the voyage: Galen, a veteran mercenary still unsure of his long-term path, and Hob, a salty and pessimistic hunter ill-adjusted to perpetual damp. Joining them was Father Lachlan, a cheerful and curious priest who had taken to life among magi with unusual ease. As they rounded the northern coast of Scotland, rough weather gave way to clearer skies—just as the uncanny began. The Double Sun Near the Orkney Isles, Nequam became aware of a powerful magical aura suffusing the sea. The crew’s senses sharpened: light seemed to pierce more clearly, and a second sun appeared on the eastern horizon. Nequam, experienced with regiones, realized this was no illusion. The false sun was not a reflection, but a gateway. Halting the ship, he cast Intellego Vim and confirmed it: the doubled sun marked the threshold into another realm. Despite reluctance from the crew, Nequam ordered the Maelstrom’s Maw forward. As they passed into the regio, the veil shimmered like water without substance. The world beyond was dazzling—sunlight suspended in the air like glistening droplets, reflecting endlessly across wave and sky. The water sparkled unnaturally, yet the horizon remained open sea. Birds and fish had vanished. Nothing stirred, except the eerie light. Nequam ordered the anchor dropped. The crew, unsure whether this was sorcery or sanctum, readied weapons and muttered prayers. No land was in sight. Descent Nequam proposed a dive. He cast Lungs of the Fish upon himself, Father Lachlan, and Galen. They followed the ship’s anchor into the depths. As they descended, the sea retained its strange clarity, but offered little else—until they found it. The anchor had embedded itself in a massive, translucent membrane—a structure like a bubble the size of a city gate. Its skin resisted the anchor’s bite without rupturing, flexing but not tearing. Nequam, drawn by its presence, reached forward and passed through. He vanished instantly. From above, Lachlan and Galen saw the mage disappear into the glowing sphere. Passage Through the Regio The seas south of the Hebrides were restless, but not with storms—something shimmered below, a place apart. Diving once more beneath the waves with magic to breathe and endure, Nequam pressed downward into an invisible layer of effervescent water, entering a realm suffused with power. The water here felt alive, fizzing against his skin like celebratory wine, sparkling and strange. There was no up or down. Only radiance. Beyond the veil, the world warped. Bands of green and violet light moved across a wide sea-space, like northern lights submerged. Hanging in the stillness were dozens—hundreds—of spherical microcosms, each a glowing orb the size of a room, suspended in liquid sky. Some pulsed like hearts. Others shimmered faintly with inward light. All of them held mysteries. The Swarm Drawn to the nearest sphere, Nequam tried to swim—but the physics of this place betrayed him. Water didn’t behave here. A kick sent him spiraling at an odd angle, drifting sideways past bubble after bubble. Then he was not alone. A flurry of creatures enveloped him—dog-sized seahorses of radiant color and curious eyes. They spiraled around him in laughing murmurations, voices overlapping in a chorus of excited questions: “What are you?” “Why are your teeth like that?” “Have you eaten yet?” “Are you new?” He answered as best he could, summoning a simple vortex of water in his hand as a display of magic. The realm reacted. Light flared. The air sang with unseen currents. The swarm shrieked with joy. Warnings and Whimsy The seahorses had no hierarchy, no leader—only momentum. But they knew fear. There was a name: Sursynth . A presence. A predator. A thing that “eats,” they said, with no more specificity than that. When Nequam gestured toward a larger bubble, they followed, flitting about him like butterflies. “Is it dangerous?” he asked. “Yes,” they chimed, delighted. “Yes, yes, yes.” The bubble’s membrane resisted touch—firm but pliable, like skin. One of the seahorses dove into his sleeve, squirmed, then emerged and declared, “Inside looks like outside!” as if it were great news. Nequam hesitated. This place—this whole realm—was built of concentric mysteries. Even its predators were peculiar. The Great Crab and the Hungry Sphere Then came the crab. It was enormous—twenty feet across, spindled and slow, drifting across the gulf between bubbles like a spider on threads. As Nequam watched, the crab moved toward a distant sphere. The orb yawned open, impossibly, and swallowed it whole. The bubble snapped shut. Inside, the creature thrashed. It did not escape. Nequam recoiled, instincts screaming. “I need to leave,” he muttered. The swarm made no effort to dissuade him, only asked for seaweed snacks and babbled about rain and teeth. He closed his eyes and willed himself to rise—mentally reaching toward the surface, threading thought with magic and memory. The realm obeyed. Return He surfaced near Father Lachlan and Galen, emerging with a gasp. The others had begun to worry—he had vanished for what felt like hours. Unable to speak underwater, he pointed up, motioning frantically. Together, they ascended to the surface. Aboard the Maelstrom’s Maw, Nequam barked for the captain. “Mark this place,” he said, still shivering. “We will return—when we are better prepared.”

Nequam’s Voyage North

The Maelstrom’s Maw sailed north along the English coast, bound for the Hebrides. The elementalist magus Nequam remained cloistered in his tarp-covered shipboard lab, barely emerging except to bark orders at the captain or issue magical instructions. Unlike Dustin's carefully orchestrated trade routes, Nequam left the provisioning and navigation to the crew. The journey became one of incidental trade and self-directed exploration, a loose course charted more by whim and weather than design.

Two grogs accompanied the voyage: Galen, a veteran mercenary still unsure of his long-term path, and Hob, a salty and pessimistic hunter ill-adjusted to perpetual damp. Joining them was Father Lachlan, a cheerful and curious priest who had taken to life among magi with unusual ease. As they rounded the northern coast of Scotland, rough weather gave way to clearer skies—just as the uncanny began.

The Double Sun

Near the Orkney Isles, Nequam became aware of a powerful magical aura suffusing the sea. The crew’s senses sharpened: light seemed to pierce more clearly, and a second sun appeared on the eastern horizon. Nequam, experienced with regiones, realized this was no illusion. The false sun was not a reflection, but a gateway. Halting the ship, he cast Intellego Vim and confirmed it: the doubled sun marked the threshold into another realm.

Despite reluctance from the crew, Nequam ordered the Maelstrom’s Maw forward. As they passed into the regio, the veil shimmered like water without substance. The world beyond was dazzling—sunlight suspended in the air like glistening droplets, reflecting endlessly across wave and sky. The water sparkled unnaturally, yet the horizon remained open sea. Birds and fish had vanished. Nothing stirred, except the eerie light.

Nequam ordered the anchor dropped. The crew, unsure whether this was sorcery or sanctum, readied weapons and muttered prayers. No land was in sight.

Descent

Nequam proposed a dive. He cast Lungs of the Fish upon himself, Father Lachlan, and Galen. They followed the ship’s anchor into the depths. As they descended, the sea retained its strange clarity, but offered little else—until they found it.

The anchor had embedded itself in a massive, translucent membrane—a structure like a bubble the size of a city gate. Its skin resisted the anchor’s bite without rupturing, flexing but not tearing. Nequam, drawn by its presence, reached forward and passed through.

He vanished instantly.

From above, Lachlan and Galen saw the mage disappear into the glowing sphere.

Passage Through the Regio

The seas south of the Hebrides were restless, but not with storms—something shimmered below, a place apart. Diving once more beneath the waves with magic to breathe and endure, Nequam pressed downward into an invisible layer of effervescent water, entering a realm suffused with power. The water here felt alive, fizzing against his skin like celebratory wine, sparkling and strange. There was no up or down. Only radiance.

Beyond the veil, the world warped.

Bands of green and violet light moved across a wide sea-space, like northern lights submerged. Hanging in the stillness were dozens—hundreds—of spherical microcosms, each a glowing orb the size of a room, suspended in liquid sky. Some pulsed like hearts. Others shimmered faintly with inward light. All of them held mysteries.

The Swarm

Drawn to the nearest sphere, Nequam tried to swim—but the physics of this place betrayed him. Water didn’t behave here. A kick sent him spiraling at an odd angle, drifting sideways past bubble after bubble.

Then he was not alone.

A flurry of creatures enveloped him—dog-sized seahorses of radiant color and curious eyes. They spiraled around him in laughing murmurations, voices overlapping in a chorus of excited questions: “What are you?” “Why are your teeth like that?” “Have you eaten yet?” “Are you new?”

He answered as best he could, summoning a simple vortex of water in his hand as a display of magic. The realm reacted. Light flared. The air sang with unseen currents.

The swarm shrieked with joy.

Warnings and Whimsy

The seahorses had no hierarchy, no leader—only momentum. But they knew fear.

There was a name: Sursynth. A presence. A predator. A thing that “eats,” they said, with no more specificity than that. When Nequam gestured toward a larger bubble, they followed, flitting about him like butterflies.

“Is it dangerous?” he asked.

“Yes,” they chimed, delighted. “Yes, yes, yes.”

The bubble’s membrane resisted touch—firm but pliable, like skin. One of the seahorses dove into his sleeve, squirmed, then emerged and declared, “Inside looks like outside!” as if it were great news. Nequam hesitated. This place—this whole realm—was built of concentric mysteries. Even its predators were peculiar.

The Great Crab and the Hungry Sphere

Then came the crab.

It was enormous—twenty feet across, spindled and slow, drifting across the gulf between bubbles like a spider on threads. As Nequam watched, the crab moved toward a distant sphere. The orb yawned open, impossibly, and swallowed it whole.

The bubble snapped shut.

Inside, the creature thrashed. It did not escape.

Nequam recoiled, instincts screaming. “I need to leave,” he muttered. The swarm made no effort to dissuade him, only asked for seaweed snacks and babbled about rain and teeth. He closed his eyes and willed himself to rise—mentally reaching toward the surface, threading thought with magic and memory.

The realm obeyed.

Return

He surfaced near Father Lachlan and Galen, emerging with a gasp. The others had begun to worry—he had vanished for what felt like hours. Unable to speak underwater, he pointed up, motioning frantically. Together, they ascended to the surface.

Aboard the Maelstrom’s Maw, Nequam barked for the captain. “Mark this place,” he said, still shivering. “We will return—when we are better prepared.”

title: Meeting in Bruges
notes: Called by Dagmar.
body_text: Summoning After Solving’s disappearance, Dagmar summons the rest of the covenant to Bruges. Some of the magi are so new that this potentially doesn’t seem unusual yet. He explains the situation, and they proceed to discuss logistics, tribunal politics, trade, vis, and when and where to meet next. Misc Notes, details, points of discussion: Vis In the Normandy Tribunal you have four sources of vis Seisins : You have to be able to walk there and walk back with the vis in a single day from your covenant. How does your covenant interpret this? Legacies : Basically, grandfathered but is too far to count as a seisin. Tropaeum : All the rest are divvied out to covenants every 7 years at the tribunal based on a tournament Luctatio : These are challenging sources, so if you can claim it, it's yours, but there's no ongoing claim; whoever can get it next time gets it There are rumors of an "Order of Odin" Books are also awarded at the tourney of the Normandy Tribunal in addition to vis; however, they are not your property, they are the tribunal's, as are any copies (this is a peripheral code situation; other tribunals have different additions to the code) Last tourney/Normandy tribunal was 1216. Charter updates Dagmar at the meeting in Bruges: "I suggest that, for the moment, we avoid telling anyone outside the covenant about Solving's temporary absence. Without an elder magus in the covenant, others, both magical and mundane, may see this as an opportunity to impose their authority upon the group. I'm particularly concerned about members of the Normandy Tribunal, who may feel that they may engage in raiding of our vessels and resources with impunity. For that reason, we should be sure to impress upon our covenant members that, while unexpected, this is only a temporary situation and not otherwise out of the ordinary. We don't want our crews to start rumors that our founder is somehow lost to us. With luck, by the time Solving returns from his quest, none will have realized he was gone in the first place.” Tribunal law allows raiding of non-magical goods between covenants, opening up possibilities for piracy or legal privateering. They explore the loophole in vis claims: anything reachable within a day on foot is "yours"—but what if you start from a ship? This sparks clever rules-lawyering potential. Reviewed seasonal duties (e.g. Éogan is handling the Kraken’s Egg vis source). The Charter: Revisiting Solving’s Vision Players discussed how much of Solving Epicurusson’s original vision should remain in effect now that he’s absent. Key tensions included: Whether to keep or temporarily suspend the Elder Magus clause (used only to break voting ties) Whether this version of the charter is permanent or provisional until Solving returns. The idea of rotating or assigned mediators—players floated giving that role special privileges (and responsibilities) General consensus leaned toward respecting Solving’s vision but acknowledging their right to revise. Covenant Structure and Seasonal Duties The group discussed how to manage: Fair wages for grogs , even if initially symbolic due to budget concerns Codifying a season of work per year per magus, whether vis harvesting, item creation, or diplomacy Covenant-wide contributions and what counts as “shared” versus “personal” magical work The Mobile Library and Central Port A core discussion revolved around the fleet’s library and winter arrangements: Consensus formed that the library would likely be housed on The Tide of Memory —Solving’s former ship, now Dagmar’s—until further notice Players agreed on Bruges as the default winter port , with flexibility to change seasonally by vote Concerns were raised about redcaps struggling to find them, prompting a suggestion for a “mailbox port” or consistent place for messages This solidified Bruges as the social and political heart of the covenant—even if informally. Normandy Tribunal and Legal Piracy This session also featured deeper parsing of Hermetic law: The covenant is part of the Normandy Tribunal , which permits raiding of mundane (non-magical) resources between covenants. The players now consider this a possible income stream A major question arose about what counts as “copying” a book under Tribunal law. Could a tapestry count? A song? Players leaned into the absurdity with glee, knowing full well the Tribunal might have opinions They also debated the “walkable in a day” vis claim clause, wondering how it applies from a ship, and leaned toward exploiting the ambiguity. The party confirmed: Dagmar has inherited the summoning bell and astrolabe from Solving’s ship and thus controls emergency coordination across the fleet Next Meeting Winter in Bruges. A New Crew Member The grogs return to The Scholar’s Wake , bringing with them a child who gives them the same weird feeling as Dustin. The child had asked to join their crew. Dustin immediately senses their gift as a magical poking, like pressure against the Parma Magica . Dustin asks their name (Stijntje Kuiper), about their parents (”I’m orphaned”) and their aptitude (they’ve clearly had some education). He accepts them on the ship but indicates that they will continue their education rather than work with the sailors.
body_html:
Summoning

After Solving’s disappearance, Dagmar summons the rest of the covenant to Bruges. Some of the magi are so new that this potentially doesn’t seem unusual yet. He explains the situation, and they proceed to discuss logistics, tribunal politics, trade, vis, and when and where to meet next.

Misc Notes, details, points of discussion:

Vis

In the Normandy Tribunal you have four sources of vis

Seisins: You have to be able to walk there and walk back with the vis in a single day from your covenant. How does your covenant interpret this?
Legacies: Basically, grandfathered but is too far to count as a seisin.
Tropaeum: All the rest are divvied out to covenants every 7 years at the tribunal based on a tournament
Luctatio: These are challenging sources, so if you can claim it, it's yours, but there's no ongoing claim; whoever can get it next time gets it

There are rumors of an "Order of Odin"

Books are also awarded at the tourney of the Normandy Tribunal in addition to vis; however, they are not your property, they are the tribunal's, as are any copies (this is a peripheral code situation; other tribunals have different additions to the code)

Last tourney/Normandy tribunal was 1216.

Charter updates

Dagmar at the meeting in Bruges: "I suggest that, for the moment, we avoid telling anyone outside the covenant about Solving's temporary absence. Without an elder magus in the covenant, others, both magical and mundane, may see this as an opportunity to impose their authority upon the group. I'm particularly concerned about members of the Normandy Tribunal, who may feel that they may engage in raiding of our vessels and resources with impunity. For that reason, we should be sure to impress upon our covenant members that, while unexpected, this is only a temporary situation and not otherwise out of the ordinary. We don't want our crews to start rumors that our founder is somehow lost to us. With luck, by the time Solving returns from his quest, none will have realized he was gone in the first place.”

  • Tribunal law allows raiding of non-magical goods between covenants, opening up possibilities for piracy or legal privateering.
  • They explore the loophole in vis claims: anything reachable within a day on foot is "yours"—but what if you start from a ship? This sparks clever rules-lawyering potential.
  • Reviewed seasonal duties (e.g. Éogan is handling the Kraken’s Egg vis source).

The Charter: Revisiting Solving’s Vision

Players discussed how much of Solving Epicurusson’s original vision should remain in effect now that he’s absent. Key tensions included:

  • Whether to keep or temporarily suspend the Elder Magus clause (used only to break voting ties)
  • Whether this version of the charter is permanent or provisional until Solving returns.
  • The idea of rotating or assigned mediators—players floated giving that role special privileges (and responsibilities)
  • General consensus leaned toward respecting Solving’s vision but acknowledging their right to revise.

Covenant Structure and Seasonal Duties

The group discussed how to manage:

  • Fair wages for grogs, even if initially symbolic due to budget concerns
  • Codifying a season of work per year per magus, whether vis harvesting, item creation, or diplomacy
  • Covenant-wide contributions and what counts as “shared” versus “personal” magical work

The Mobile Library and Central Port

A core discussion revolved around the fleet’s library and winter arrangements:

  • Consensus formed that the library would likely be housed on The Tide of Memory—Solving’s former ship, now Dagmar’s—until further notice
  • Players agreed on Bruges as the default winter port, with flexibility to change seasonally by vote
  • Concerns were raised about redcaps struggling to find them, prompting a suggestion for a “mailbox port” or consistent place for messages

This solidified Bruges as the social and political heart of the covenant—even if informally.

Normandy Tribunal and Legal Piracy

This session also featured deeper parsing of Hermetic law:

  • The covenant is part of the Normandy Tribunal, which permits raiding of mundane (non-magical) resources between covenants. The players now consider this a possible income stream
  • A major question arose about what counts as “copying” a book under Tribunal law. Could a tapestry count? A song? Players leaned into the absurdity with glee, knowing full well the Tribunal might have opinions
  • They also debated the “walkable in a day” vis claim clause, wondering how it applies from a ship, and leaned toward exploiting the ambiguity.

The party confirmed:

  • Dagmar has inherited the summoning bell and astrolabe from Solving’s ship and thus controls emergency coordination across the fleet

Next Meeting

  • Winter in Bruges.

A New Crew Member

  • The grogs return to The Scholar’s Wake, bringing with them a child who gives them the same weird feeling as Dustin. The child had asked to join their crew.
  • Dustin immediately senses their gift as a magical poking, like pressure against the Parma Magica.
  • Dustin asks their name (Stijntje Kuiper), about their parents (”I’m orphaned”) and their aptitude (they’ve clearly had some education). He accepts them on the ship but indicates that they will continue their education rather than work with the sailors.

title: Solving’s Disappearance
body_text: Reinier (silent sellsword), Willem (bluff crew chief), Pieter (stammering former surgeon), Leofwin (grizzled cook) Solving is at a table with the grogs. Rainier keeps watch. Pieter goes to the bar to buy a drink. Willem brings four ales back for the group, grinning. As Willem returns, he notices a subtle glow framing Solving. Within 15 seconds, it intensifies— brilliant light floods the tavern , and Solving vanishes before their eyes. (Rainier) “Is that something he does very often?” Rainier checks the back alley , finding clutter and debris but no trail. Inside, the group regathers, shaken. Lufwin had missed the moment while chatting up the barkeep, but saw the flash and now notices Solving’s absence. The patrons grow increasingly curious. The grogs discuss the strange occurrence in hushed tones. Back at the ship, Dagmar is informed. Dagmar believes Solving has entered Twilight , based on past similar episodes—short absences followed by cryptic revelations. (Dagmar) “Yes, he’ll be back. Take me to where you left him. Back at the tavern, Dagmar refuses to leave . He tells the grogs: “I’d like to be here when Solving returns so that the experience is fresh in his mind. I’ve heard about these things. The bartender grows uncomfortable. Willem tries to get Dagmar to return to the ship. (Dagmar) “My behavior? My behavior’s fine. What’s wrong with my behavior?” Pieter, Willem, and Leofwin form a buffer to give Dagmar space and keep tensions with the tavern staff low. (Leofwin) “Well.” (He takes out a piece of paper, scribbles a note) “For Solving. No one else.” (Places it where Solving vanished) Over the next four days , grogs rotate duty to escort Dagmar to and from the tavern. Emotions vary: Dagmar : Increasingly confused. “Someone’s lost the script. And it’s not me.” Peter : Pragmatic. “Just a job.” Willem : Stressed, trying to reassure Dagmar—“No, no, he’ll be back.” Reinier : Detached. Thinks: “Magi do crazy shit. We just wait.”

Reinier (silent sellsword), Willem (bluff crew chief), Pieter (stammering former surgeon), Leofwin (grizzled cook)

Solving is at a table with the grogs. Rainier keeps watch. Pieter goes to the bar to buy a drink. Willem brings four ales back for the group, grinning.

As Willem returns, he notices a subtle glow framing Solving. Within 15 seconds, it intensifies—brilliant light floods the tavern, and Solving vanishes before their eyes.

(Rainier) “Is that something he does very often?”

Rainier checks the back alley, finding clutter and debris but no trail. Inside, the group regathers, shaken. Lufwin had missed the moment while chatting up the barkeep, but saw the flash and now notices Solving’s absence.

The patrons grow increasingly curious. The grogs discuss the strange occurrence in hushed tones.

Back at the ship, Dagmar is informed.

Dagmar believes Solving has entered Twilight, based on past similar episodes—short absences followed by cryptic revelations.

(Dagmar) “Yes, he’ll be back. Take me to where you left him.

Back at the tavern, Dagmar refuses to leave. He tells the grogs:

“I’d like to be here when Solving returns so that the experience is fresh in his mind. I’ve heard about these things.

The bartender grows uncomfortable. Willem tries to get Dagmar to return to the ship.

(Dagmar) “My behavior? My behavior’s fine. What’s wrong with my behavior?”

Pieter, Willem, and Leofwin form a buffer to give Dagmar space and keep tensions with the tavern staff low.

(Leofwin) “Well.” (He takes out a piece of paper, scribbles a note)

“For Solving. No one else.” (Places it where Solving vanished)

Over the next four days, grogs rotate duty to escort Dagmar to and from the tavern. Emotions vary:

  • Dagmar: Increasingly confused. “Someone’s lost the script. And it’s not me.”
  • Peter: Pragmatic. “Just a job.”
  • Willem: Stressed, trying to reassure Dagmar—“No, no, he’ll be back.”
  • Reinier: Detached. Thinks: “Magi do crazy shit. We just wait.”

title: Sorting through Solving’s letters and documents / Finding ‘V’
body_text: Correspondence Solving Contact, “V” Ship is Ready Finding V? Correspondence Dagmar discovered the following correspondence: Solving Contact, “V” To Solving Epicurusson, (by the hand of Mercere or other trusted courier) You may not recognize the hand, but you will remember the words. We last corresponded—briefly—regarding the vis dispute off the coast near Saint-Valery, where your fleet’s interests touched upon the holdings of a Tytalan recluse. You spoke, then, of building something new upon the water. I answered with a question about how the Code would fare beneath the tide. I write now in earnest. You once had a contact in Leuven—one who offered you access to the Duke’s private seals, and who quietly urged caution when the Rhine Quaesitors began asking after your interests. I am that man, though my title has since been revoked, and my name carries weight only as a cautionary tale in Tribunal chambers. The Rhine has become untenable. The air is thick with rumors, and knives no longer need justification. There has been no vote, not yet, but the outcome—should it come to one—is foretold. I do not need the Tribunal to tell me what I am, or what I must become to survive. You spoke once of a covenant in motion, unanchored and burdened less by the weight of Tribunal demands. I ask now: does that offer still stand? I am in Bruges. I will remain within sight of Saint Jacob’s bell tower, near the fish-market stairs, for three more cycles of the moon. Burn this letter. —V. Ship is Ready To the Esteemed Members of the Sjórseiðr, I write with satisfaction and a touch of pride to inform you that the final ship commissioned—fifth in your remarkable fleet—is now fully completed and seaworthy. She lies docked in our shipyard in Bergen, awaiting your representatives for delivery and final inspection. The vessel is constructed according to the specifications agreed upon with Master Solving Epicurusson, whom we have not heard from in some weeks. As such, we request clarification on who will be receiving her and attending to the matter of final payment reconciliation. Our books show modest adjustments to the balance, owing to refinements made during construction, which we will gladly review with your representative. It has been an honor to build for your covenant. Each ship has posed its own challenge, and each one, I hope, carries with it a bit of the North Sea’s soul. May she serve you well in your ventures. Please advise us of the name under which this vessel shall be entered in our records, and who shall captain her henceforth. In good faith and fellowship, Bjørn Erlingsson Master Shipwright of Bergen Anno Domini 1220 Finding V? Rumors indicate that a man matching the description was abducted by men in the livery of the Duke of Brabant . Duchy of Brabant – Just east of Bruges, stretching toward what is now modern Belgium and the Netherlands. Its capital was Leuven (Louvain), and it was an important center of trade and culture in the early 13th century. It is, unhelpfully, inland. It would be considered to be in the Rhine , rather than the Normandy, Tribunal. Dagmar recruits Garrat Coffin , along with grogs Pieter van Dijk and Reinier , to investigate discreetly. Garrat gathers intelligence from locals, prostitutes, and dockworkers, uncovering: A description of the missing man: sharp-faced, Roman nose, dark hair, well-dressed , paranoid. A silver brooch left behind—possibly an arcane connection. A local prostitute named Alix had it in her possession: the stone in it is not precious, but carefully polished, and the amount (and quality) of silver is quite small. Nonetheless, Dagmar is able to ascertain a weak residual magical aura: this was worn by a magus, for some time, and not long ago. (using “What is up with this brooch?” Intelligo Vim ) Pieter tries to negotiate access to city guards (the Stadswacht), ultimately arranging for them to visit the holding cells and records . Despite his stammer and compulsive lying flaw, Pieter eventually succeeds. He was the “surgeon for a local prominent person” Dagmar uses Pose the Silent Question on the clerk in the room with the holding cells. Confirms the Duke’s men removed someone without city sanction; and that is significant; Baron Arnulf van Maele would not be happy to learn this . They reconvene at the ship. Dagmar is pursuing some arcane possibilities for how to find this mysterious ‘V’.
body_html:
Correspondence
Solving Contact, “V”
Ship is Ready
Finding V?

Correspondence

Dagmar discovered the following correspondence:

Solving Contact, “V”

To Solving Epicurusson,
(by the hand of Mercere or other trusted courier)

You may not recognize the hand, but you will remember the words.

We last corresponded—briefly—regarding the vis dispute off the coast near Saint-Valery, where your fleet’s interests touched upon the holdings of a Tytalan recluse. You spoke, then, of building something new upon the water. I answered with a question about how the Code would fare beneath the tide.

I write now in earnest.

You once had a contact in Leuven—one who offered you access to the Duke’s private seals, and who quietly urged caution when the Rhine Quaesitors began asking after your interests. I am that man, though my title has since been revoked, and my name carries weight only as a cautionary tale in Tribunal chambers.

The Rhine has become untenable. The air is thick with rumors, and knives no longer need justification. There has been no vote, not yet, but the outcome—should it come to one—is foretold. I do not need the Tribunal to tell me what I am, or what I must become to survive.

You spoke once of a covenant in motion, unanchored and burdened less by the weight of Tribunal demands. I ask now: does that offer still stand?

I am in Bruges. I will remain within sight of Saint Jacob’s bell tower, near the fish-market stairs, for three more cycles of the moon.

Burn this letter.
—V.

Ship is Ready

To the Esteemed Members of the Sjórseiðr,

I write with satisfaction and a touch of pride to inform you that the final ship commissioned—fifth in your remarkable fleet—is now fully completed and seaworthy. She lies docked in our shipyard in Bergen, awaiting your representatives for delivery and final inspection.

The vessel is constructed according to the specifications agreed upon with Master Solving Epicurusson, whom we have not heard from in some weeks. As such, we request clarification on who will be receiving her and attending to the matter of final payment reconciliation. Our books show modest adjustments to the balance, owing to refinements made during construction, which we will gladly review with your representative.

It has been an honor to build for your covenant. Each ship has posed its own challenge, and each one, I hope, carries with it a bit of the North Sea’s soul. May she serve you well in your ventures.

Please advise us of the name under which this vessel shall be entered in our records, and who shall captain her henceforth.

In good faith and fellowship,
Bjørn Erlingsson
Master Shipwright of Bergen
Anno Domini 1220

Finding V?

  • Rumors indicate that a man matching the description was abducted by men in the livery of the Duke of Brabant.
    • Duchy of Brabant – Just east of Bruges, stretching toward what is now modern Belgium and the Netherlands. Its capital was Leuven (Louvain), and it was an important center of trade and culture in the early 13th century. It is, unhelpfully, inland.
    • It would be considered to be in the Rhine, rather than the Normandy, Tribunal.
  • Dagmar recruits Garrat Coffin, along with grogs Pieter van Dijk and Reinier, to investigate discreetly.
  • Garrat gathers intelligence from locals, prostitutes, and dockworkers, uncovering:
    • A description of the missing man: sharp-faced, Roman nose, dark hair, well-dressed, paranoid.
    • A silver brooch left behind—possibly an arcane connection. A local prostitute named Alix had it in her possession: the stone in it is not precious, but carefully polished, and the amount (and quality) of silver is quite small. Nonetheless, Dagmar is able to ascertain a weak residual magical aura: this was worn by a magus, for some time, and not long ago. (using “What is up with this brooch?” Intelligo Vim)
  • Pieter tries to negotiate access to city guards (the Stadswacht), ultimately arranging for them to visit the holding cells and records.
    • Despite his stammer and compulsive lying flaw, Pieter eventually succeeds.
    • He was the “surgeon for a local prominent person”
  • Dagmar uses Pose the Silent Question on the clerk in the room with the holding cells.
    • Confirms the Duke’s men removed someone without city sanction; and that is significant; Baron Arnulf van Maele would not be happy to learn this.
  • They reconvene at the ship. Dagmar is pursuing some arcane possibilities for how to find this mysterious ‘V’.

title: The Kraken’s Egg
notes: 5 Animal vis Advancement total: 5 XP Auram (Adventure)
body_text: Continuity note: this takes place before the meeting in Bruges. Éogan’s Dream Éogan awakens from another vivid dream. In it, he swims deeper and deeper into an iridescent void, surrounded by coalescing stars and colors that shift like kelp in current. He walks a regal procession through a palace of seashell and light, courtiers whispering around him. At the throne waits a queenly figure of radiant tendrils and indescribable beauty. A hermit-like creature offers him a pearl from an oyster, and a voice declares: “The dowry is nearly complete. I cannot wait for us to be wed.” When Éogan accepts the pearl, he feels a rush of power. Upon waking, he finds the pearl in his hand—small but potent—and recognizes it as similar to an earlier dream-gift. A magical theory check reveals the pearl may be slightly tainted, capable of causing warping. A second pearl from a previous dream seems likewise affected. Bergen Éogan, aboard the Brineborn, prepares for the season’s task: following a kraken to obtain its magical egg. He recalls witnessing the process once before, during his macgnímartha under Solving Epicurusson’s guidance. This year, he returns to familiar kraken-haunting waters and seeks signs along the coast near Bergen. In town, Éogan hears only sailor’s tales until a merchant, Master Erlingson, reveals an awaiting ship, commissioned by Solving: a knarr, equipped for a mage, with a lab compartment under the central tarps. Caught off guard, Éogan promises payment and postpones retrieval, then inquires further about kraken sightings. Erlingson mentions a fjord a few days’ sail to the north. With Erc, a grog who knows some Norwegian, Éogan asks along the coast. While rumors are vague, the merchant’s tip proves useful. The kraken and Ka’wa’ill Sailing toward the fjord, Éogan begins to sense a magical aura. For Erc and Drest, the grogs, the scene feels sharpened—brightened by unnatural light. The sun seems to pierce their heavy cloaks, while nearby birds and sea life vanish, replaced by eerie stillness. Éogan detects a strange scent, growing stronger as they near a nexus of magic. Soon, a pod of whales breaches the surface. Beneath the waves, Ka'wa'ill—a merfolk exile who despises slavery—observes the pod and the arrival of an enormous kraken. Though he has never seen one, the beast’s scale and presence overwhelm him. Curious about the nearby ship, Ka'wa'ill swims up to investigate. Éogan, meanwhile, dons his Eyes of the Merfolk spell and dives. He and Ka'wa'ill see each other—two out-of-place beings meeting beneath the surface. The kraken has affixed itself to a rocky nook near the seabed. Back aboard the Brineborn, Éogan signals the crew and confirms their proximity to the beast. He spots Ka'wa'ill again, now at the surface, and attempts communication. Switching languages, he discovers the merfolk understands some heavily accented Gaelic. Despite early confusion—“fish with a man’s body,” “man eaten by a fish”—the two establish basic mutual respect. Ka'wa'ill warns of danger: “Big monster. Very bad.” Éogan explains they intend to follow the kraken and retrieve its egg, using illusions and gestures. Ka'wa'ill misconstrues this as Éogan possibly wanting to marry the kraken, but eventually understands the goal. The attack began without warning. A single tentacle burst from the waves and coiled around the back third of a surfacing whale, followed swiftly by a second. Within moments, the enormous creature began to thrash, its head briefly visible above water before it was dragged downward in a violent churn of foam and blood. The other whales scattered—some charging in futile defense, others fleeing out to sea. From the Brineborn, the crew watched in stunned silence as the water churned with carnage, Éogan issuing firm commands to keep the ship at a safe distance. Ka'wa'ill, watching from the far side of the vessel, shielded by the hull, tracked the kraken’s movements in grim awe. For hours afterward, the water remained unsettled, the brutal majesty of the scene leaving a lasting imprint on the crew. The kraken then pushed out to sea. They follow the kraken’s path for ten days, led in part by Ka'wa'ill swimming ahead with his trident aloft. The magical aura fades, and Ka'wa'ill recalls nursery rhymes from his childhood that warn of fae danger in such areas. When he voices concern—“Bad. Very bad.”—Éogan is wary but presses on. At last, they arrive at an undersea volcanic cone. Though dormant, it seems to suit the kraken, which coils itself on the slope. The next day, Éogan is drawn toward strange water-creatures that leap like spirits across the moonlit sea—he recognizes them as faerie beings and resists their luring. The kraken dives into the depths. Ka'wa'ill follows and sees the egg, nestled beneath a rocky lip. He alerts Éogan, who casts Lungs of the Fish , dons lighter clothes, and dives with Ka'wa'ill. The egg is large but light, floating upward when freed. The two guide it carefully back to the Brineborn. As they reach the surface, Éogan triumphantly hoists the egg from the water. The crew, stunned, cheers. Ka'wa'ill then asks to come aboard. As the sailors ready a net, Ka'wa'ill transforms mid-haul, his fish tail becoming human legs. Naked and unbothered, he walks the deck for the first time. The grogs fetch clothes, and Éogan leads him into the lab, gifting him a pawn of vis, though Ka'wa'ill doesn’t yet know what to do with it. The expedition complete, Éogan plans to spend the next season practicing Latin. Ka'wa'ill, curious and eager to learn, stays aboard to study the ways of humans.

title: The Summer Fog
notes: 5 Mentem vis (only 4 obtained)
body_text: The Fog Dustin had been tasked with a dangerous harvest: Mentem vis drawn from an annual fog known to haunt a coastal village. The mist, born of some subtle enchantment or curse, did not simply obscure—it whispered, invaded, clung to dreams. It brought nightmares. Armed with sailcloth nets stretched between trees, a prepared spell, and quiet resolve, Dustin set his trap. Villagers helped in silence, but their unease was palpable. Children were sent inland. Fields were left fallow. The wiser among them remembered past years and vanished early. The rest waited just beyond the ridge, turning dread into festivity. Warding the Village It came without wind. The mist did not swirl or drift—it advanced, deliberate and low, like a tide. Dustin stood ready. When the first tendrils touched the nets, he invoked his magic. Rego Aquam shaped the fog, bound it in momentary circles of force. Wineskins were stoppered with bottled fear. More vis clung to the nets, beaded along ropes like dew. The work was delicate. Magic captured two pawns. The nets would yield two more. Heynric’s Fall Heynric, watching from a low hill, began to feel it. Not the press of spellcraft, nor a curse—something older. Inside the mist, his mind turned against him. Unbidden memories surfaced. Childhood fears. Night-terrors once buried. The fog did not speak, but it knew him. He bolted. Crashing through the nets, Heynric tore the cloth and brought one line down, choking in the cold. Vis clung to his face, its raw form laced with nightmare. Cynthia rushed to his side as he flailed. For a moment, he was not a sailor or a scholar, but a boy again, hunted by ghosts. It passed. Heynric, recovered. The fog rolled on.

Dustin had been tasked with a dangerous harvest: Mentem vis drawn from an annual fog known to haunt a coastal village. The mist, born of some subtle enchantment or curse, did not simply obscure—it whispered, invaded, clung to dreams. It brought nightmares.

Armed with sailcloth nets stretched between trees, a prepared spell, and quiet resolve, Dustin set his trap. Villagers helped in silence, but their unease was palpable. Children were sent inland. Fields were left fallow. The wiser among them remembered past years and vanished early. The rest waited just beyond the ridge, turning dread into festivity.

Warding the Village

It came without wind. The mist did not swirl or drift—it advanced, deliberate and low, like a tide. Dustin stood ready. When the first tendrils touched the nets, he invoked his magic.

Rego Aquam shaped the fog, bound it in momentary circles of force. Wineskins were stoppered with bottled fear. More vis clung to the nets, beaded along ropes like dew. The work was delicate. Magic captured two pawns. The nets would yield two more.

Heynric’s Fall

Heynric, watching from a low hill, began to feel it.

Not the press of spellcraft, nor a curse—something older. Inside the mist, his mind turned against him. Unbidden memories surfaced. Childhood fears. Night-terrors once buried. The fog did not speak, but it knew him. He bolted.

Crashing through the nets, Heynric tore the cloth and brought one line down, choking in the cold. Vis clung to his face, its raw form laced with nightmare. Cynthia rushed to his side as he flailed. For a moment, he was not a sailor or a scholar, but a boy again, hunted by ghosts.

It passed.

Heynric, recovered. The fog rolled on.

body_text: As summer waned and autumn approached in the year 1220, Dagmar found himself adrift—both physically aboard the Tide of Memory , and emotionally, following the disappearance of his master, Solving. Still struggling to accept that his mentor may never return, Dagmar busied himself with what he knew best: inquiry, analysis, and the pursuit of magical understanding. Yet, even in this focus, there remained a tension—between grief, the drive to prove himself, and the persistent mystery of the missing mage "V". Earlier efforts to trace this mysterious figure—who had been arrested or vanished amid political entanglements in Bruges—had borne little fruit. An attempt to establish an arcane connection from an item recovered at a brothel failed. The Duchy of Brabant’s mundane authorities were suspected of interference, but lacking a direct link, Dagmar could only speculate. Reluctantly, and likely at Solving’s unseen urging, Dagmar decided to leave Bruges and sail north once more. The plan: to explore potential magical regio sites off the coasts of Norway and Sweden, further away from Tribunal scrutiny. Yet Dagmar did not spend this time idly. Recognizing a gap in his corpus knowledge—a hindrance in his previous investigative efforts—he set to remedy it. Onboard the Tide of Memory , Dagmar announced a new research direction and requisitioned assistance from the crew. He selected grogs at random and requested that they assist with "anatomical and magical studies." This resulted in a series of bizarre, deeply unsettling (for the grogs) but highly productive experiments. Dagmar had always been strange, but this series of sessions elevated his eccentricity. He asked grogs to disrobe and perform synchronized calisthenics—arms flailing, backs pressed together, twisting and contorting in near-comical ritual movements. His muttered observations, arcane diagrams, and furious scribbling became infamous among the ship’s complement. "Back to back! Now spin!" he cried, ink quill darting as he watched for signs of magical resonance. His notes grew stranger: diagrams of stick figures juxtaposed with sudden wind gusts, shifting sail patterns, and speculative correlations between muscle flexion and ambient aura fluctuations. Crew morale suffered, though none dared outright refuse Dagmar. His magical status—and the fervor with which he pursued his research—discouraged open complaint. Still, they whispered that Solving’s absence had finally unhinged him. “The moon’s struck him hard,” they murmured. “He watches the sail, not the spell. He listens to the wind more than the wailing.” Despite the absurdity, the experiments worked. Dagmar gained 23 experience points in the Corpus Art, raising his understanding from level 1 to 6. The research marked a turning point—an investment not only in knowledge, but in agency. He could no longer rely on Solving. If he wished to unravel the political threads surrounding V, or to pursue the deeper mysteries of regio and the North Sea’s untamed magic, he would need to stand on his own. Notably, Dagmar was also the only mage who remembered that the Aegis of the Hearth had not been cast since Solving’s disappearance. With winter approaching and the covenant preparing to reconvene in Bruges, Dagmar silently committed himself to learning or coordinating the necessary rituals. He could no longer assume someone else would handle the essentials. While others trained grogs, learned languages, or planned trade routes, Dagmar was drawing anatomical sketches of sailors mid-spin, watching cloud movements, and muttering to himself beneath the deck’s lantern light.

As summer waned and autumn approached in the year 1220, Dagmar found himself adrift—both physically aboard the Tide of Memory, and emotionally, following the disappearance of his master, Solving. Still struggling to accept that his mentor may never return, Dagmar busied himself with what he knew best: inquiry, analysis, and the pursuit of magical understanding. Yet, even in this focus, there remained a tension—between grief, the drive to prove himself, and the persistent mystery of the missing mage "V".

Earlier efforts to trace this mysterious figure—who had been arrested or vanished amid political entanglements in Bruges—had borne little fruit. An attempt to establish an arcane connection from an item recovered at a brothel failed. The Duchy of Brabant’s mundane authorities were suspected of interference, but lacking a direct link, Dagmar could only speculate. Reluctantly, and likely at Solving’s unseen urging, Dagmar decided to leave Bruges and sail north once more. The plan: to explore potential magical regio sites off the coasts of Norway and Sweden, further away from Tribunal scrutiny.

Yet Dagmar did not spend this time idly.

Recognizing a gap in his corpus knowledge—a hindrance in his previous investigative efforts—he set to remedy it. He selected grogs at random and requested that they assist with "anatomical and magical studies." This resulted in a series of bizarre, deeply unsettling (for the grogs) but highly productive experiments.

Dagmar had always been strange, but this series of sessions elevated his eccentricity. He asked grogs to disrobe and perform synchronized calisthenics—arms flailing, backs pressed together, twisting and contorting in near-comical ritual movements. His muttered observations, arcane diagrams, and furious scribbling became infamous among the ship’s complement.

"Back to back! Now spin!" he cried, ink quill darting as he watched for signs of magical resonance. His notes grew stranger: diagrams of stick figures juxtaposed with sudden wind gusts, shifting sail patterns, and speculative correlations between muscle flexion and ambient aura fluctuations.

Crew morale suffered, though none dared outright refuse Dagmar. His magical status—and the fervor with which he pursued his research—discouraged open complaint. Still, they whispered that Solving’s absence had finally unhinged him. “The moon’s struck him hard,” they murmured. “He watches the sail, not the spell. He listens to the wind more than the wailing.”

Despite the absurdity, the experiments worked. Dagmar gained 23 experience points in the Corpus Art, raising his understanding from level 1 to 6. The research marked a turning point—an investment not only in knowledge, but in agency. He could no longer rely on Solving. If he wished to unravel the political threads surrounding V, or to pursue the deeper mysteries of regio and the North Sea’s untamed magic, he would need to stand on his own.

While others trained grogs, learned languages, or planned trade routes, Dagmar was drawing anatomical sketches of sailors mid-spin, watching cloud movements, and muttering to himself beneath the deck’s lantern light.

title: The handoff of the Maelstrom’s Maw
body_text: Kor, a newly introduced Flambeau magus, was brought into the campaign via a flashback-esque retelling. He met Nequim in the Hebrides. Nequim, eager to divest himself of obligations, offered Kor ownership of his ship and Covenant responsibilities in exchange for a vague promise of future compensation or partnership. Kor describes Nequim as “generous, kind, magnificent” while clearly having been suckered into a raw deal. Establishes Kor’s character as a wandering, justice-driven knight-errant who disdains tournaments but respects martial virtue.

Fire From the Sky
notes: All magi are generally involved in this, but they can also perform a compatible season activity. 10 Terram vis result.
body_text: A deadly hailstorm drops burning granite spheres into the northern sea. The stones lose their vis if not collected by dawn . Gathering for the Meteor Storm Ships converge using magical and mundane navigation. Plans are made to collect the Terram vis meteors: Magi cast Lungs of the Fish or use the Brooch of the Fish. Swimmers include Garrett, Udo, Kawa’il, and a Dutch beefcake named Bruno. Dagmar remains on deck to spot and direct meteor landings. The Meteor Storm Spells like Clear Sight of the Naiad , True Sight of the Air , and Cloak of Duck Feathers (which Éogan botches) are cast. Flaming meteorites rain down. Swimmers recover them with gloves, nets, or sacks. Ka’wa’il impresses with his merfolk tail; Garrett tries to compete with him. Kor dives after a meteor and experiences severe magical nausea as he approaches a submerged massive rib —part of a huge magical beast. He touches it and casts an Intelligo-Animal spell, discovering it's a rib from a magical leviathan-sized creature (~30 km in length). Sky Ship Crash As the storm rages, a ship crashes from the sky , hitting the Maelstrom’s Maw. Valdemar , a skyclad Viking war-magus, had been lost in a regio for centuries. He emerges as the sole survivor—his crew reduced to skeletons. He had tried to call a storm to return home and partially succeeded. The impact damages both ships but miraculously neither sinks. Valdemar is confused, shocked to learn it is the 13th century, and his fleet (and era) are long gone. Post-Crash Chaos & Salvage Magi rush to help. Dagmar and Kor are able to communicate with Valdemar in Latin, and are surprised that he seems to be hermetic, albeit of the dead House Diedne. Valdemar is examined for signs of the Gift and Parma Magica—confirming he's a genuine Diedne lineage magus. Language barriers are navigated (Gaelic, Norse, Latin). Valdemar eventually realizes he’s been time-displaced ~400 years. He mourns the war and kingship he missed. Valdemar casts spontaneous Rego Aquam to freeze seawater and temporarily patch his hull. Dagmar and Kor agree it's unsafe to remain. The region in the sky has disappeared, but the aura below remains. The party agrees to winter in Bruges to repair ships and process the implications. Kor wants to return to study the site in winter, but Dagmar insists on waiting for spring. Analysis of the Aura and Creature Dagmar uses magic to track the submerged rib and concludes it belongs to a giant magical sea serpent or leviathan. Aura strength fluctuates with depth, following the skeleton’s submerged body.

title: Flying Fortress
body_text: Since the covenant is seaborne and has no landed estates, they rely only on trade. Kor proposes enchanting a giant stone disk (about 20 acres) and constructing floating islands for farming, silk caterpillars, eel ranching, or crafts. Rationale: ships are fragile and insufficient for long-term magical work. This would allow building “towers that can fly and go where needed.” Éogan: skeptical if it’s possible, almost nonsense. Dustin: open but worried a dispel effect could cause catastrophic collapse. Kor’s answer: Trigger condition: “if not flying, then re-engage effect.” Thus, a dispel only causes momentary fall before reactivating. Floating islands could also be made from pumice cones filled with soil. Mobility: as fast as Rego magic propulsion—comparable to ships. Éogan: This is a long-term project; immediate focus should be short-term profitability to stabilize the covenant before building infrastructure. Dustin: Infrastructure will take coin they don’t have; covenant is “in the hole.” Kor’s calculation: ~ 18 pawns of vis to create a 20-acre disk . Possible to complete in two seasons (with prep). Could be finished in about 1 year if lab totals improve slightly. Éogan surprised it’s less costly than expected. Éogan: How defend it while absent? Kor: Altitude prevents mundane attack. Main threats: mystical creatures (griffins, winged beasts). If flying over water, threats are reduced. Éogan proposes charter rule: one covenant member must guard the fortress per season as their service obligation. Discussed: A 70-year invested device vs a lesser enchantment . Lesser enchantment only requires matching lab total (not ×2). Enchantment level: ~33 . Kor estimates he needs +1 in Magic Theory to pull it off. Biggest issue isn’t vis, but mundane site/labor —clearing, infrastructure, costs. Kor’s answer: Build an outdoor lab on a large cleared plot. Use Creo to create the granite ring. Steps: 2 seasons to conjure stone. 2 more seasons to enchant. ~3-year project total. Flying Fortress: Step 1, Building a Hanger In order to build a flying ship, fortress, or castle you need to build the object first. Then you need to enchant it. This can take as little as one season, but it requires the darn thing to fit in your lab Thus, if you want to build a flying castle, you must first construct some some of "lab space" that the castle can fit inside. This can be as much as a large clearing in the woods, or a massive underground hanger that you simply delete the ceiling once your mission is complete. This prepared space is, make no mistake, purely temporary. For our purposes, i'm a modestly broke wizard. Renting out land, or squatting would present the problems of evoking the ire of the people who possibly own the land, much less the efforts it would take to properly level out and clear 23 odd acres. You could use some fallow farmland, and do it the winter, using a magical ward to keep snow and the elements out. An alternative, is to just make a floating island and use the same method of protects to shield you from the elements while you conjure forth and enchant an entire castle. The math The area in meters for 23 acres is roughly 93077 m. As a perfect square, each side would be 305m in length, giving us a max radius of about 150m. For the initial disk, I want a radius of 50m. The disk is essentially a slice of a cylinder, as such the volume calculations pertinent for designing the spell is V = πr²h. 50 is a neat number for this, we get a thickness of 1.27 and a volume of 1000. For the spell to make this disk, because quarrying a solid disk of stone would be tedious and time consuming, the spell is as follows CrTe 20 R R: Touch, D: instant, T: Individual Create the Obsidian Disk This ritual creates a perfect Obsidian disk. Kor's sigil creates an obsidian where the streaks of purple flicker and wave across the obsidian like liquid fire frozen. Base 3, +1 Touch, +3 size, +1 intricacy (shape) The second shape, the ring, is 10 levels higher, for 100 times the volume in cubic paces For the second spell, the disk that surrounds the initial one, which will encompass the rest of the space, will fit around the first so the interlock almost. CrTe 30 R Create the Granite Ring This spell creates a ring of granite that's total radius is 150m, and inner radius starts at 50m, so that it interlocks with Kor's Obsidian Disk. The granite is rife with various strata that mimic the flickering of flame due to Kor's Sigil. R: Touch, D Instant, T: individual Base 3, +1 touch, +5 size, +1 intricacy ( shape) Now that the rings are made, which is cast and done in a days time, It takes 2-3 seasons to enchant them all. The Second ring is the easiest, it can be enchanted as a lesser device, which only takes a single season. A lesser device doesn't need to be opened for enchantment first. burrowing the lab text from legends of Hermes page 123, a disk 300 paces long and 1 pace wide can be enchanted to fly with a level 33 enchantment, costing only a measly 4 pawns of terram vis. `` The flight disk ReTe 33 pen 0, Constant effect This item accepts a number of predefined command phrases in latin, I.e. Disk, Height set 10 Paces up, Disk, Move 10 paces East and South. Thus the outer disk is not very maneuverable. The environmental trigger, for it to trigger automatically without command, is if the spell is not working. Since the effect is immediate, it does not make the flight jerky. Effect: Base 3, +1 Diameter, +3 size, +1 affect Stone, Modifications + 10 unlimited uses, Environmental Trigger +3 Lab total Needed : 66 70 Is pretty high, especially for one season. The Shape and material bonus will have to do some work, in addition, we're going to add a 70 year expiry to this enchantment to double our lab total. assuming 10 Creo, 10 Terram, 5 magic theory, an experimentation bonus of 3, and the bonus of inventive genius(3), 2 int, we get a lab total of 33, doubled is 66. The second, inner disk, Kor will open as his talisman, this takes a season to attune, and a season to enchant, which is more costly. Starting with opening it with 6 pawns of vim, and enchanting a similar effect for 4 more terram vis. All in all, it costs 6 pawns of vim, and 18 pawns of terram vis to create two flying disks. The biggest hurtle will be securing a space to use as a workshop, but once done, the covenant will have access to a roughly 20 acre sized flying disk for development and use. Of note, the hollow center of the outer disk could be used as a bay to create similar objects afterword. For the vim vis I can allocate seasons of extracting vis from an aura. It will delay the plan indeed.

title: Learning the Aegis of the Hearth for the Sjórseiðr covenant / Studying Vim
notes: Aegis failed, Vim raised from 3 ⇒ 5
body_text: Dagmar wants to learn Aegis of the Hearth . He can read the Latin, but true understanding requires observing it in action. He uses Intellego Vim to study the covenant’s active Aegis as a guide. He does not complete his studies this season. Unique twist: their Aegis applies not to a fixed location but to a fleet of ships and their crews. This innovation raises rules questions, but the GM allows it. Winter attempt fails: totals ~10 points short. He pivots to raising Vim: studies via Dustin’s magical pig, raising Vim from 3 → 5.

Tribunal Politics & Raiding

  • Valdemar mocks “modern” shipbuilding compared to his drakkar (shallow-draft, portage-capable). Others counter with larger trade capacity.

body_html:
Heynric's Mission to Limburg - Spring 1221

The Setup

The covenant is operating on credit and needs a loan extension. Their financier Bernard in Bruges explained the problem: the Duke of Limburg has been their backer, but the Duchess is conservative about money and prefers "sedentary" investments rather than ventures. Heynric must travel to Limburg to convince them to loosen the purse strings.

The Party

Heynric assembled a delegation:

  • Heynric - The merchant/negotiator (companion)
  • Father Lachlan - Franciscan priest (played by Daniel)
  • Henri - Failed apprentice, teacher, socially awkward (played by Matt/Dustin - there was some confusion)
  • Leonhardt - Grizzled veteran soldier (played by Jim, new character)

The Journey

The journey of a couple hundred kilometers was primarily by river. The group got along well - three extroverts (Heynric, Father Lachlan, Henri) and one taciturn veteran (Leonhardt). Languages were managed as Heynric spoke German and French, Father Lachlan had various languages, and the Duke and Duchess spoke Low German and French.

Heynric explained the financial situation openly: the covenant needs money to cover expenses while still in the red. The problem isn't the business case - Heynric can present that expertly - but convincing someone who doesn't think in terms of investment.

Arrival in Limburg

Upon arrival, they took a day to recover and reconnaissance:

Heynric's Investigation (rolled 15 on gossip/townsfolk):

  • Limburg is a distribution hub, not a production center
  • Trade flows from Cologne to Bruges to Limburg, then gets divided for county-level distribution
  • The Duke shows "beneficent indifference" to trade
  • He periodically showers favored projects with money, then has periods of austerity
  • The Duke never cuts spending on hunting trips
  • The Duke is currently on a hunting trip (away for 1-2 weeks)

Father Lachlan's Investigation (rolled 9):

  • There's been a recent moral panic about Albigensianism/Cathars
  • One person with clear Gnostic beliefs was forced out
  • This caused additional accusations and paranoia about heresy
  • The Duchess is very devout and concerned about Christian stewardship

Heynric's Follow-up (difficulty 7, rolled 13):

  • He located the Duke's hunting lodge through careful conversation
  • Had to reveal he represents merchants of "uncanny abilities" seeking funding
  • Learned the Duchess's religious devotion is a major factor in her financial conservatism

The Plan

The group decided to go directly to the Duke at the hunting lodge rather than wait or deal with the Duchess. This would give them an audience without her conservative influence.

Henri's Investigation (rolled amazing with gossip):

  • The Duchess loves birds, especially exotic ones
  • A special parrot had just arrived from far away that speaks French phrases
  • The parrot says "bien dit" (well said) and repeats "Ave Maria"
  • Henri's cat Might was introduced to the caged parrot - after initial wariness, they got along

The Trek to the Hunting Lodge

The group decided to walk rather than use horses (horses don't actually speed travel, just reduce exhaustion). This proved problematic:

The Journey (various stamina rolls):

  • Father Lachlan (survival skill) tried to guide them but struggled with their inexperience
  • Heynric and Henri had never camped or traveled long distances on foot
  • They had minimal supplies - just wineskins, basic packs
  • Leonhardt scouted ahead and spotted wild boars (the Duke's hunting grounds)
  • They carefully avoided the boars with spears drawn
  • Henri critically failed, slipping while trying to be stealthy, tumbling down a hill
  • Henri sustained a twisted ankle, light wound, and two levels of fatigue
  • They limped to the lodge with Henri supported by the others

Meeting the Duke

As they arrived at the lodge, the Duke's hunting party returned with a slain stag. The Duke is described as similar to Robert Baratheon from Game of Thrones - big, boisterous, loud.

The Audience:

  • They were given rough accommodations in the servants' area (but at least beds!)
  • Had an hour to clean up and prepare
  • Were seated "below the salt" at dinner - not servants but not honored guests

Advice Given to Heynric:

  • Henri: Use flattery with nobles
  • Father Lachlan: Thank him for his graciousness and the dinner
  • Leonhardt: Be short and direct - this is a fighting man who wants straight talk

Heynric's Approach:

  • Decided to be witty and charming rather than purely businesslike
  • Would read the room and get direct if needed
  • Keep the Duke in a good mood since he's doing what he enjoys

The Presentation (rolled 9 on charm, difficulty 3):

  • The introduction went extremely well
  • The Duke became familiar quickly, in a jovial mood from successful hunting and drinking
  • Heynric laughed at the Duke's jokes, the Duke laughed at his

The Pitch (rolled 15 on bargain, difficulties 7 and 9):

  • Presented it as a wonderful opportunity in its foundation stages
  • Needed the Duke's support to build something truly amazing
  • Emphasized they didn't want to act without the Duke's permission
  • Would be to the Duke's advantage and credit

The Duke's Solution:

  • Explained his funds are tied up in his wife's anti-Cathar work
  • Doesn't want to interfere with that
  • But - the hunting season was extraordinarily successful
  • He'll dip into his personal hunting fund to finance it directly
  • His personal purse isn't accounted for the same way as joint finances
  • Result: A letter signed by the Duke worth 250-300 mythic pounds (enough to carry the covenant for several years)

Aftermath

  • The group's status was elevated - now "at the salt" rather than below it
  • They stayed one more day (Heynric conflicted between not wanting to walk back vs. knowing things could only go downhill)
  • Father Lachlan tried to inquire about the expelled Cathar (failure - people don't know details but don't suspect him)
  • Henri found a walking stick for the return journey
  • They successfully returned to Bruges with the letter

title: Series B Funding with Bernard
body_text: Bernard’s office: bustling clerks, stuffy tomes, Bernard himself (salt-grey, precise). Heinrich pitches: income doubled, routes improved, ships well-provisioned. A Bargain roll succeeds. Bernard recognizes Heynric’s family name ( Baert ) and asks about ties to the Duchess of Limburg. Bernard explains: Duke of Limburg is his main investor, but the Duchess insists on “sedentary money.” Funds are frozen unless she can be swayed. He offers to extend credit once she loosens her grip. If not, he’ll refer them to competitors. Afterward, Éogan worries: involvement with nobility is risky. Heynric accepts but plans to gossip-gather about the Duchess (background, temperament, religion) before acting. Likely allies: Father Lachlan, Isabeau Foxglove.

body_html:
Valdemar's Mission - Retrieving the Kraken's Egg

The Setup

Every year, a kraken surfaces in the North Sea (between Norway and Scotland), lays a single egg, and if retrieved within a certain timeframe, the egg is worth 5 pawns of Animal vis rather than hatching. This is a resource no other covenant claimed.

The Crew

  • Valdemar - Ex-Bjornaer mage, former Viking/pirate, captain
  • Ka’wa’ill - Warrior merman, learning language slowly (played by Daniel)
  • Leofwin - Retired pirate, now covenant cook with renewed enthusiasm (played by Matt)
  • Garrat - Adventurer with sharp smile and combat focus (played by Dustin)

Crew Dynamics

  • Leofwin: Finally on a "real" ship - fighting men who can sail, not sailors who can fight. Excited about the merman and Valdemar's pirate background. Has his cutlass sharpened and weapons ready.
  • Garrat: Competitive, always looking for adventure or trouble. Has "greater immunity to deprivation" - doesn't suffer from lack of air, food, or drink (but can't regain fatigue without them).
  • Ka’wa’ill: New to this world above water, fascinated by mages, wants to test himself against Garrat in combat (after the mission).
  • Valdemar: Collaborative leader, doesn't hold himself above his crew. Pragmatic - looks for mundane solutions before magical ones. Open to plunder if opportunities arise.

The Fae Encounter - Night Before Arrival

Valdemar's Dream:

  • Found himself swimming deeper into darkness with iridescent colors
  • Entered an underwater corridor with pearls, shells, beautiful light
  • Saw his "bride" - fair-haired, proper curves, dressed as a Northern noble lady
  • She said "my love, it's been so long" and mentioned giving "someone who looked like you" some of his dowry
  • Presented three pearls with vis in them
  • They embraced and consummated the marriage

Valdemar's Realization (rolled 13 on Faerie Lore):

  • Mid-encounter, noticed things were wrong - couldn't see parts of her body, movements were impossible
  • Realized this was Fae magic, but also knew:
    • Faeries aren't necessarily malevolent, just alien and lacking creativity
    • They're following a story/pattern
    • The smoothest way out is to play along to completion
    • Interrupting them badly could be dangerous

First Failed Attempt:

  • Valdemar asked about "the rest of your kingdom" - trying to extend the story
  • Rolled a botch (0) - realized immediately this was a mistake
  • Was giving her new story directions that would further entangle him

Second Attempt:

  • Praised the wonderful wedding and evening
  • Said he must return home but would see her again "someday" (open-ended, no new story)
  • Made a guile/communication roll (details of result not given but he escaped)
  • Woke up underwater at ~200 meters depth, caught in Fae nets

The Underwater Rescue

Morning Discovery:

  • Valdemar was missing from the ship
  • Ship anchored (standing procedure - don't sail at night in dangerous waters)

Ka’wa’ill's Reconnaissance (rolled 3 on North Sea Lore):

  • Transformed to fish form to scout
  • This area is equivalent to a "dead zone with sand worms" - extremely dangerous
  • Saw wave riders (horse-like fae) galloping across the surface
  • At 200 meters: Fae nets made of captured memories
  • Spotted a human form in the second net down

Planning:

  • One brooch of water breathing available (Father Lachlan/Leofwin can use it)
  • Garrat has immunity to deprivation (can hold breath indefinitely without damage)
  • Decided: Leofwin takes brooch, all three go down

The Rescue:

  • Found a large bioluminescent jellyfish creature with Valdemar tangled in its tentacles
  • Ka’wa’ill used "Voice of the Ocean" to direct Atlantic cod (1.5-2 meters long)
  • Cod shredded through the nets (not the tentacles)
  • Jellyfish retreated, releasing Valdemar
  • Valdemar woke underwater, disoriented, started swimming up desperately

Valdemar's Escape:

  • Rolled botch on swimming (only one botch die)
  • Made stamina roll (barely - rolled 3, needed 3)
  • Realized: ~8 minute swim to surface, only seconds of air, increasing panic
  • Cast spontaneous Muto Aquam spell (level 5, silent, exaggerated gestures)
  • Created "water rocket boots" effect
  • Shot to surface in 85 seconds at ~5 mph
  • Made two more stamina rolls (rolled 6 - success with botch die meaning 3 days recovery)
  • Experienced mild "bends" from rapid ascent

Aftermath:

  • Garrat menaced the jellyfish creature with his sword, severing one tentacle
  • All four surfaced safely
  • Valdemar found the three pearls with aquam vis on his bed
  • Successfully retrieved the Kraken's egg without further incident

The Revelation - Winter 1221

Valdemar's Confession:

  • Showed the pearls to Éogan and other mages
  • Asked what obligation he'd entered into
  • Explained the encounter

Éogan's Response:

  • Had similar encounters twice before
  • Was told "the betrothal was almost ready"
  • Never progressed to Valdemar's situation
  • No idea what the creature wants or how to exit the situation

Valdemar's Memory (rolled 9 with confidence on intelligence):

  • Remembered: Before the time jump (400 years ago), he'd had a dream
  • Met this woman, offered to marry her

Your covenant lands fall clearly within the new Tribunal's domain by ancient right—the old Carolingian borders that Rome herself acknowledged. We offer you covenant-right in the founding charter, full brotherhood in our council, and protection under the new Peripheral Code we shall establish. Send Brother Calvinus your answer before the feast of All Saints. The new age comes whether you stand with us or remain chained to the past. Letter 1

To our Brothers of Scarem Montem,
In Hermes' Name and by the Bonds of Art

Worthy Sodales,

The time for half-measures and careful words hath passed. We write to you plainly, as befits magi who would reshape the very foundations of Hermetic law.

The Lotharingian Tribunal shall be born, whether the dotards of Rhine and the raiders of Normandy will it or no. Already have seven covenants of the Rhine pledged their support, and our own liege Florum leads the Normandy faction with Spider's Palace in full accord. Come the next Grand Tribunal, we shall present our petition with such force that none may gainsay it.

Yet we have need of your covenant's strength to make this vision complete. Montverte hath been your liege these many years, true enough, but what profit have you gained from this bondage? When did they last aid you in your hour of need? When did they share their plunder from raids upon defenseless covenants? They treat you as servants, not as brothers.

Join with us, and you shall be founding members of a new Tribunal where your voice shall carry weight equal to any. Your vis sources shall be confirmed by charter—no more fear that some upstart covenant might claim what lies within a day's march of your walls. Your place at Tribunal shall be secured by right, not by the whims of ranking votes.

Rhesus of Verditus hath already drawn the boundaries. Your covenant lands fall clearly within the new Tribunal's domain by ancient right—the old Carolingian borders that Rome herself acknowledged. Montverte cannot drag you into foreign territory against your will, nor by any law of the Order.

We offer you covenant-right in the founding charter, full brotherhood in our council, and protection under the new Peripheral Code we shall establish. In return, we ask only that you declare for the Lotharingian cause when the moment comes to act. No treachery is required—merely the courage to claim what is rightfully yours.
Send Brother Calvinus your answer before the feast of All Saints. The new age comes whether you stand with us or remain chained to the past.

Written in the Season of Harvest, Anno Domini 1221

For the Magi of Spider's Palace,

—Rhesus of Verditus
—Calvinus of Jerbiton

Letter 2

To the Worthy Magi of the Covenant Scarem Montem,
Greetings in the name of Hermes Trismegistus

Brothers in Art,


I write from the dungeons of Duke Henry of Brabant, where I am held upon charges most spurious, having been delivered here by treachery of mine former sodales. Though my body be confined, my will remains free, and I have urgent need of intelligence concerning one who was to be my new brother-in-arms.
Know that I had sworn oath to join the maritime covenant Sjórseiðr under their leader, one Solving Epicurusson. We were to meet at the feast of St. Michael past, yet when I arrived at the appointed place, no sign of him could be found. Mine former covenant-brothers—may their names be cursed—seized upon this absence to arrange my present circumstance through their agents in the Duke's court.


I have reason to believe that your covenant hath had commerce with this Solving, whether in trade of vis, books, or other needful things. If this be so, I beseech you most earnestly: tell me where he may be found, or if he yet lives, or what manner of business hath kept him from our agreement.


For I fear greatly that he hath abandoned me to mine enemies by design, and if this be proven true, then by the ancient laws of our Order I must challenge him to certamen that this matter be settled with honor. A magus who betrays his sworn word deserves no mercy beneath the stars.


If you aid me in this matter, I shall remember it well when I am free of this place—as I shall be, whether by law or by Art. The Rhine magi think themselves clever, but they have awakened a serpent that will not sleep again until justice is sated.


Send word by any means you deem safe. Time grows short, and my patience shorter still.


Written by mine own hand in the Year of Our Lord 1221, in the fourth month


—Valerian de Castellane of the House of Guernicus
