body_html:
The Raid on the Hound of Cassel - Summer 1221

The Setup

Following discussions about funding the covenant through legitimate trade and opportunistic piracy, Valdemar received intelligence about a prime target: the Hound of Cassel, a merchant vessel belonging to a covenant that relies heavily on sea trade. The ship was scheduled to sail from England to Dunkirk, likely carrying valuable correspondence between covenants as well as trade goods.

The Raiding Party

Valdemar assembled his crew:

  • Valdemar - Viking captain and rune mage (magus)
  • Ka’wa’ill - Atlantean ally maintaining human illusion (companion)
  • Garrett - Strong English fighter (grog)
  • Giden and Leofwin - Named crew members
  • Additional Viking warriors - Mix of experienced raiders

The Plan

Intelligence Gathering (Valdemar rolled well on survival/navigation):

  • Mapped the likely route from English ports to Dunkirk
  • Identified that medieval merchants prefer coastal routes, anchoring nightly
  • Found an uninhabited stretch of coastline with a concealed lagoon
  • Determined the merchant ship likely lacked oars (Viking advantage)

The Ambush

Valdemar positioned himself at the prow, staff raised, and proclaimed: "You will heed my will. You will obey my commands. You will be still. For I am the Runemaster of the winds, and I command you, be still!"

  • The wind spirits obeyed (whether cowed or amused)
  • The merchant vessel's sails went slack
  • Vikings deployed oars and closed rapidly

Initial Contact:

  • Grappling hooks thrown to bind ships
  • Valdemar had crew shout in French, German, and Flemish
  • His broken English message: "Drop your arms and you'll live, fight and you'll die!"
  • Some merchants understood, creating division in their ranks

The Battle

  • Initiative slightly favored the merchants
  • Both sides vaulted railings to board
  • Ka’wa’ill maintained his human illusion throughout
  • Valdemar knocked into water early (failed defense)
    • Spent turn climbing back aboard
    • Dramatically vaulted back over railing, blade extended

Ka’wa’ill’s Struggle:

  • Took medium wound from axe-wielding sailor
  • Opponent tried hooking him with axe "beard" to pull overboard
  • Eventually used superior positioning to push attacker into water
  • Realized: "these humans wear armor for a reason"

Garrett's Ordeal (multiple wound rolls):

  • Sustained 2 medium wounds, 1 light wound (-7 penalty total)
  • Nearly overwhelmed when double-teamed
  • Valdemar charged to rescue: "Get off my buddy!"
  • Managed to force one attacker overboard with superior footwork

Resolution:

  • Viking rear secured first
  • Fighting pushed to merchant vessel
  • Several merchants threw down weapons
  • Victory achieved but at significant cost

The Prize

The Ship:

  • Debate whether to keep as prize or sink
  • Decision to find "shadow port" for sale

Discovered Cargo (Valdemar rolled well on awareness/search):

  • Textiles and pigments
  • Glass bottles (valuable oddities)
  • Bolts and practical supplies
  • Colorful items and jewelry
  • Three magically sealed boxes (suspicious - to be opened on merchant ship)
  • Bundle of correspondence (most valuable find)

The Intelligence

The correspondence revealed:

  • Evidence of conspiracy between covenants
  • Plans for rigging tribunal contests
  • Letters about the Lotharingian Tribunal formation
  • A desperate message from imprisoned Valerian de Castellane

Aftermath

Medical Situation:

  • Valdemar and Garrett both severely wounded
  • Months of recovery needed
  • Ship's chirurgeon to provide care
  • Both on light duty only

Prisoner Handling:

  • Surrendered crew released on shore as promised
  • Dead: "They fought too hard and got themselves killed. I warned them."

Strategic Outcome:

  • Intelligence worth more than physical treasure
  • Proof of concept for piracy operations
  • Need to "lay low" after successful raid
  • Three sealed boxes saved for later examination

body_html:
Tribunal Invitation

The liege covenant Montverte will host the 1223 Normandy Tribunal.

The Magically-Sealed Chests from the Hound of Cassel

The Dilemma

  • Captured three magically sealed chests from the ship
  • Legal Status: "Fuzzy area" - not a clear code violation
  • Opening them wouldn't be a sure violation but would require adjudication
  • Could be considered "natural resources" raiding (permitted under Normandy rules)
  • Even scrying to see inside might violate code

Proposed Solutions

  1. Wait and See: Hold them until the 1228 tribunal (7 years away)
    • "If they don't mention it by then, finders keepers"
    • Time-honored tradition of hoping problems go away
  1. Return Discreetly: Leave them on doorsteps like foundlings
    • Avoid potential tribunal charges
    • Maintain good relations
  1. Use as Leverage: Return them in exchange for something

Risk Assessment

  • Scarem Montem might know where the chests are and come looking
  • Could result in settlement negotiations or tribunal adjudication
  • Covenant decides to hold them for now, prepared to return if questioned

Discovery of Valerian de Castellan

  • Who: Valerian de Castellan of House Wernicus (Quaesitores - the law enforcement/judges of the Hermetic Order)
  • Location: Imprisoned by the Duke of Brabant in Breda (his seat of power in Brabant fief)
  • Discovery Method: Letter found on the captured ship during the naval battle

Benefits to Rescuing

Multiple strategic reasons discussed:

  1. Political Leverage: Having a Quaesitor (Hermetic judge/lawman) as ally/debtor
  1. Covenant Strength: Add powerful magus to their ranks
  1. Avoiding Enemy: Better than having a prosecutor with a grudge
  1. Opportunity: They have funding from Duke of Limburg and a "deniable" ship

Jurisdictional Complications

  • Important Discovery: Brabant is in Rhine Tribunal territory, not Normandy
    • Can't leverage Normandy tribunal connections for help
    • Different peripheral code may apply
    • Must avoid negative attention to the Order
    • Less political cover if things go wrong

Strategic Challenges Identified

  • Not a Sea Raid: Castle infiltration completely different from ship capture
  • Need Subterfuge: Can't fight their way in through the front gate
  • Extraction Plan: Must assume they can sneak in but may have to fight their way out
  • Timeline: No specific deadline, but Valerian's letter suggests urgency

The specifics of what to do are unclear, as whether Valerian is being held civilly, criminally, or in connection to an offense against the church will change dynamics substantially.

Decision is made to send a forward party with Dagmar, with the intent of following up in the spring to retrieve Valerian.

Lotharingian Tribunal

Scarem Montem has been reached out to, but it’s been intercepted.

There’s a Rhine/Normandy secession crisis brewing.

The magi struggled to think of precedent; Transylvanian Tribunal was new territory; Loch Leglean was a secession but it is remote/peripheral.

Most likely this will be brought forward at the Grand Tribunal in 1228.

Notable that Florum and its vassal covenant, Spider’s Palace, are in support. There is no mention of Montverte, the liege of Scarem Montem. Montverte would be very interested in the letter they intercepted.

The group decides to be non-interventionist, at least for now. Valdemar strongly opposes giving up their current arrangement. The others argue that their current autonomy may not persist.

Kor’s Absence

With the 1223 Normandy Tribunal approaching - the first the young magi would attend as gauntleted wizards - Valdemar called for a strategic planning session. The covenant needed to determine their goals and capabilities for this crucial political and competitive event.

The Council

Present for discussions:

  • Valdemar - Seeking Diedne resources and vengeance
  • Dustin
  • Éogan
  • Dagmar

Understanding the Tribunal

Structure Explained:

  • Regional gathering dividing resources and settling disputes
  • Convention side for politics
  • Tournament side for resource allocation
  • The Normandy Tribunal uses contests to award vis sources and books
    • Library Books: Must be returned; copies also become tribunal property

The Book Controversy:

  • Discovery that copied books remain tribunal property sparked outrage
  • "I copy it and you still call it yours? Bullshit!"
  • Group resolved to change this law at tribunal

Tournament Analysis

The Six Traditional Events:

  1. Hastiludium - Athletic/physical competition
  1. Certamen - Wizard duels (mental forms, not combat magic)
  1. The Joust - Mounted combat
  1. The Melee - Group combat
  1. Dimicatio - "Forceless casting," most dangerous
  1. Host's Choice - Variable

Scoring System Review (careful analysis of standings):

  • 24 teams competing
  • Positions 22-24: Nothing
  • Position 21: 12 points (tradition to donate half)
  • Position 13: "Siege of Shame" (no prize due to 1151 scandal)
  • Position 9+: Significant rewards
  • Conclusion: Must finish at least 21st to avoid shame

Personal Agendas

Valdemar's Mission (passionate discussion):

  • Seek any Diedne resources or methodologies
  • Strategy: Use Tremere against Tytalus, then destroy both
  • Focus on spontaneous magic (what freed him from temporal prison)
  • Will challenge for any Diedne-related resources

Covenant Priorities (group consensus):

  • Books over vis sources for development
  • Practical magic items (freshwater barrels for ships)
  • Aquam resources for maritime operations
  • Laboratory texts for item creation

Capability Assessment

Event Assignments (strategic discussion):

Certamen:

  • Dagmar best suited (even scores, intellego spells)
  • Dustin could compete well

Dimicatio:

  • Dustin strongest candidate (balanced arts)
  • Owen possible but reluctant
  • Valdemar opts out: "No thanks"

Melee:

  • Valdemar primary fighter
  • Kor as secondary option
  • "Even if I don't prevail, I want to gain experience"

Joust:

  • No clear candidate
  • Valdemar: "I wouldn't know how to wield a lance"

Hastiludium:

  • Described as "medieval warfare" with a ball
  • "Closest thing to medieval warfare I've ever experienced"
  • Multiple participants possible

Political Considerations:

  • Need additional magus for voting power
  • Address the "Lotharingian problem"

The Host Question:

  • Unknown who will host
  • Host gets to choose sixth event
  • Need flexibility in preparation

At Tribunal:

  • Compete in minimum 3-4 events for participation points
  • Use intelligence for maximum leverage
  • Focus on achievable goals (21st place or better)
  • Network for future opportunities

Dustin has noticed that Stinjtje understands etiquette but has tried to not be obvious about it. Asks them about nobles and prisoners.

Stinjtje asks about where they dine; prisoner ranking determines treatment. Lets slip that a “prisoner actually ranked highly enough to dine with me father.”

Dustin asks if Stinjtje would accompany Dagmar. They are unsure, until they are reassured that the Duchy of Brabant is far enough away from Bruges.

Adam Smith and Father Lachlan will also go.

Will take a cog up to Breda for.

The group travels to the Duchy of Brabant to investigate and potentially rescue Valerian de Castellane, who appears to be held in custody. The party consists of:

  • Father Lachlan (taking lead on diplomatic approach)
  • Stintia
  • Adam Smith (reconnaissance and mapping)
  • Dagmar (staying in background to avoid complications)

Pre-Mission Briefing:

  • Dagmar provides Father Lachlan with a silver brooch as identification
  • Message to deliver: "Apologies on behalf of Solving, who was unavoidably delayed"
  • Father Lachlan notes the religious jurisdiction falls under the Bishopric of Liege, the same bishop focused on expelling Albigensian heresy they encountered in Limburg

Father Lachlan begins the infiltration with a public sermon in the town square, skillfully balancing passionate preaching with practical grace and charity. It creates an excellent impression - he strikes the perfect balance between exciting oratory and practical spiritual guidance. The local clergy welcome him warmly and offer hospitality.

Father Lachlan presents himself as:

  • A member of the Franciscan Order (Order of the Poor)
  • Following "the wind of Spirit" in his travels
  • Seeking to minister to the downtrodden, including prisoners
  • Requesting access to provide spiritual comfort to those incarcerated

Prison Reconnaissance

The local Abbot arranges for Father Lachlan to visit the prisoners, accompanied by Adam Smith (who memorizes layouts and creates mental maps for later sketching).

The Three Tiers of Imprisonment:

Lower Dungeon:

  • Nearly empty, reserved for condemned criminals
  • One murderer awaiting execution in few weeks, chained to wall
  • Conditions matching classical dungeon horror: rats, bread crumbs, darkness

Middle Tier:

  • 8-9 prisoners, mostly political/economic crimes
  • Poaching violations, unpaid debts, temporary punishments
  • Prisoners known by name to the clergy, many baptized by the elderly priest guide
  • Regular mass attendance, more humane conditions

Upper Tier - "Studio Apartments":

  • Luxurious prison suites with multiple connected rooms
  • Guards outside but comfortable conditions within
  • Two current occupants

Meeting Wilikin van Rotselaar

The first upper-tier prisoner is Wilikin van Rotselaar, a 15-year-old heir of a vassal lord.

The Confession:

Wilikin, seeing Father Lachlan as a safe outsider, requests confession and reveals:

  • Murder fantasies about escaping as a hero
  • Embarrassment over rejection by a serving girl
  • Typical adolescent struggles amplified by political imprisonment

Father Lachlan responds with:

  • War stories (which Wilikin focuses on the wrong elements of)
  • Advice about violence vs. fantasy
  • Gentle guidance about kindness and maturity
  • Seeds planted for future growth, even if not immediately sprouting

Valerian de Castellane

Initial Approach:

Father Lachlan smoothly presents the silver brooch during what appears to be routine spiritual counseling. Valerian recognizes it but remains extremely cautious, offering only minimal responses. Adam Smith notes:

  • The room contains 30+ books (astonishing for a non-library)
  • Extensive desk with papers everywhere
  • Clear signs of scholarly work
  • Adam senses the Gift - confirming Valerian is a magus

The Private Conversation:

After Valerian dismisses the local priest, the truth emerges:

Valerian's Situation:

  • Imprisoned by the Bishop of Liege, not the Duke
  • The Bishop wants him silenced (reasons not fully revealed)
  • The Duke is cooperating with the Church for unknown reasons
  • Valerian cannot trust any clergy under the Bishopric

The Revelation:
When Father Lachlan mentions their covenant, Valerian's composure breaks:

  • He collapses into a chair, shocked
  • Asks "Were you not involved in my capture?"
  • Learns that Solving was "unavoidably delayed" (Dagmar still in denial about Solving's fate)
  • Expresses bitter irony: "Better late than never"

The Message:

Valerian:

  1. Writes a note for the Covenant
  1. Casts a spell on it (openly, showing his magical nature)
  1. Seals it and hands it to Father Lachlan
  1. Refuses to provide an arcane connection (hair/fingernail) - doesn't trust them enough yet
  1. States communication methods are outlined in his missive
  1. Warns explicitly: "You cannot trust the clergy"

Dagmar's Premonition:

Upon receiving Valerian's letter, Dagmar rolled an exceptional Intelligence + Premonitions check (natural 20+), revealing two critical insights:

  1. The letter is magically booby-trapped
  1. A vision of the Duke of Brabant receiving a letter from the Pope

The Magi's Debate:

The covenant debated how to safely examine the letter:

  • Dagmar's Plan: Burn the letter under controlled conditions, then use his spell "Tales of the Ashes" to reconstruct its contents from the ashes
  • Alternative Suggestions: Have a grog open it, use spontaneous magic to analyze it first
  • Group Decision: Travel to a magical aura site on the coast to investigate using Intellego Vim magic

title: Negotiating Guillaume's two favors
notes: Dustin's letter exchange with Guillaume le Pro fixes the terms of the Montverte favor.
body_text:
Dustin sent a letter to Montverte offering to fulfill the favor owed since Solving's deal.
Guillaume le Pro of House Flambeau answered with two options: (A) deliver 5 pawns of Creo vis to the Tribunal **outside the Redcap network**, or (B) lend public diplomatic weight to Montverte's press on Dragon's Rest (vassals of Confluensis).

Communication roll: 4 (Order-of-Hermes Lore + Politics speciality) — negotiation closes cleanly.

title: Up the Sarthe to Le Mans on the Storm Dragon
notes: Bruges → Le Mans → Montverte. Éogan exploded a Push of the Gentle Wave casting and turned the upriver leg into a luxury cruise.
body_text:
The party gathered in Bruges and sailed the coast south to the mouth of the Sarthe.
Valdemar's drakar **the Storm Dragon** carried the magi inland to Le Mans. From Le Mans they hired carts overland to Montverte.
Éogan cast **Push of the Gentle Wave** to drive the ship upstream and rolled an exploding success — "a very luxurious trip," the deck barely shifting beneath them.
Magi aboard: Dagmar, Éogan, Dustin, Valdemar, Valerian, and Stijntje (apprentice).
Companions: Adam Smith (Stijntje's protector), Gerard de Mule, Valdemar's wife Rán.
Grogs (~8–10): Garrett, Drest (from the Brineborn), several unnamed.
Special: Rosie the magical pig familiar, palpably excited by the smell of distant vis caches along the route.
Not attending: Éel (depression when landlocked), Heinrich (sent trading), Solving (excuse of "other studies" — covers his Twilight disappearance).
The Brineborn (Éogan's ship) also engaged in trade over the journey.

notes: Camp set, the covenant takes stock — betting odds, factional intelligence, mission plan, and concerns.
body_text:
Political intelligence. Dagmar observed distinct nodes of magi — clusters not interacting except through intermediaries. Clear factional tensions; specifics unclear. A game of telephone running between clusters.
Betting odds. Éogan discovered the covenant is ranked #17 of 24 in the betting books — much better than expected (they had assumed bottom tier). 17th place would earn 4 prize pawns.
Awareness rolls. Éogan rolled poorly — overwhelmed by stimuli, paralysed by contradictory social expectations. Valdemar took charge of setting up camp while Éogan recovered. Dagmar rolled well — noticed the factional clustering.
Dustin's diplomatic mission plan. Track down Frettigesis and Emma on Tuesday. Need Éogan to point out where they're camped. Ensure Confluensis doesn't overhear the conversation. Don't volunteer that Montverte requested this unless pressed. Arguments to make: Confluensis is fracturing, failing to lead; better opportunities under Montverte.
Tournament strategy. Current ranking: 17th (4 prize pawns). Goal: don't aim too high — "wild success would introduce its own problems" from heavy hitters paying attention. Dagmar will scout for research contacts interested in regiones.
Valerian at the Hastiludium. Confirmed he'll participate in at least one event. His inclusion makes 5 magi total.
Concerns raised. Why avoid the Redcap network for the vis? How will Confluensis react? Want to stay independent — not become anyone's vassal.

title: Bridget of Scarem Montem's Lotharingian pitch
notes: A Scarem Montem Tremere casts an obscuring spell mid-conversation and walks Éogan through the Lotharingian secession case.
body_text:
On the free day, Éogan accepted an audience with **Bridget of Scarem Montem** (House Tremere).
Mid-conversation she began a deliberate, non-hostile casting — Éogan was given the choice to allow it; he raised an eyebrow and let it through. Obscuring spell: their words would not reach unintended ears.
Bridget's pitch: covenants on both sides of the Rhine-Normandy border are quietly preparing a **Lotharingian Tribunal**, escaping the vassal pyramid and the seven-year resource churn. She offered to **hold any Tourney winnings in jurisdictions outside Normandy's recall** if Éogan wished.
Éogan played it as personally interested while professing covenant neutrality.
Open thread: Éogan has not yet shared the conversation with the rest of the covenant.

title: Erobos of Lapis Crudus on regiones
notes: Dagmar's regio-research detour after striking out on Solving's letters. The 200-year-old Lapis Crudus scholar talks past him, but the substance is real.
body_text:
Failing to extract sense from Solving's letters, Dagmar pivoted to what he actually cares about and went looking for regio scholarship.
Found **Erobos of Lapis Crudus** — somewhere between 150 and 200 years old, looks seventy, speaks in slow deliberate paragraphs and follows his own conversational current regardless of input.
Substantive content Dagmar walked away with:
• Rarefication does not always involve physical motion — one may deepen into a regio without feeling movement.
• Transitions between regio levels can be sharp thresholds **or** gradients, and sometimes the boundary type cannot be distinguished from inside.
• Erobos's own apprentice climbed a hill that kept extending; reached intensity-5 before retreating, with no indication the levels stopped.
• A distinction worth preserving: which observations belong to a particular regio, and which seem universal.
Dagmar tried to push into epistemology (fundamental mystery vs. unsolved problem). Erobos showed a strange, genuinely uncomprehending expression and continued on his preferred track.

title: Éogan's certamen vs. Mira of Fudarus
notes: First-round draw against a Fudarus veteran. The veto trick: Mira proposed Ignem (zero), Éogan vetoed it, freeing her to fight on Mentem (nine). Loss in four rounds, but reputation gained.
body_text:
Round-of-24 draw: Éogan vs. **Mira of Fudarus**.
Éogan won initiative (rolled 6), chose Creo. Mira proposed Ignem; Éogan vetoed; Mira proposed Mentem; Éogan accepted. (Revealed afterwards by overheard crowd commentary: Mira has 0 in Ignem and 9 in Mentem — the Ignem proposal was bait.)
**Round 1.** Éogan attacked CrAq — water rising from the ground. Mira's phantasmal form turned the water into drifting flower petals (defense 13). Counter-attack difference of 6 — two fatigue levels in one exchange (Winded, Weary).
**Round 2.** Éogan attacked with Mentem — anxiety as air ripples. Mira drew a bubble; no damage. On counterattack Éogan rolled well on defense; one further fatigue level.
**Round 3.** Both rolled weakly on offense. Mira **botched** her counterattack — Éogan removed a fatigue level instead of gaining one. Tied.
**Round 4.** Éogan pressed Mentem; difference of 2; Int + Penetration just barely added a fatigue level to Mira — first successful hit. Even at the cap. Mira counterattacked with a difference of 16 — phantasmal form broke apart, reformed wrong. Éogan's head dropped; he passed out.
Crowd clapped for both. "Mira hasn't gone four rounds in a decade."
Dustin caught the veto-trick chatter in the crowd and relayed the lesson back to the table.

title: Hastiludium qualifying vs. Montverte
notes: Sled + Unseen Porter strategy. Montverte fields Ermengarde in a washtub flanked by Alzheim and Ranolf. Five rounds; Montverte spends itself on Painful Magic and folds.
body_text:
Pre-spells: **Comfort of the Drenched Traveler** (Dustin → Éogan), **Wizard's Sidestep** (Dagmar → Éogan).
Opposing team **Montverte**: **Ermengarde of Flambeau** seated in a washtub, with **Alzheim** (Auram) and **Ranolf** (Rego Mentem) as her magical assists.
Spell recon — Dagmar (Magic Theory + Per, 8): identified Alzheim's *Charge of the Angry Winds* (concentration); Ranolf's penetration-enhancing self-cast. Ermengarde's prep remained unknown.
**R1.** Dagmar rolled 17 on a stress *Unseen Porter*. Alzheim landed *Charge of the Angry Winds*. Ranolf's area sleep failed to penetrate.
**R2.** Alzheim's third *Charge* started accruing Painful-Magic fatigue. Ermengarde lurched on the wind and *Palm of Flame*'d Éogan's cart — Éogan fast-cast a CrAq to drown it, **and targeted the washtub** with *Mighty Torrent of Water*: the tub overflowed and crashed waterlogged.
**R3.** Ranolf's *Aura of Rightful Authority* surplus 26 vs. Éogan's MR 5; Éogan made the Int+Concentration save and refused to "turn around." Dustin's fire-extinguishing spont misfired (-3) but broke Alzheim's concentration anyway.
**R4.** Dustin's *Broom of the Winds* (27) flung Alzheim **South** off the field. Ranolf botched a follow-up. Ermengarde kicked out tub-slats to drain, then botched her self-propulsion and took a fatigue level.
**R5.** Alzheim's last *Charge* succeeded — pushed Ermengarde forward. Dustin laid a spontaneous **CrTe salt barrier** (Magic Focus) in her path. Ranolf's second *Aura* (total 21) failed to penetrate.
Éogan's wagon crossed the line. Alzheim collapsed in fatigue, Ermengarde's basin fell. **Sjórseiðr advances to the quarterfinals.**
Ranolf shook Éogan's hand: "Well done, sir." Dagmar offered Ermengarde *Comfort of the Drenched Traveler*; she did not decline.
Side note (Dagmar's Awareness+Communication): Montverte (the host) took the loss hard. Defeated in qualifying. Sentiment in the field: "this isn't a good look."

notes: Opponents lead with an illusory decoy vessel that races halfway across the field on round one. Sjórseiðr sees through it, deflects the hailstorm, and crosses first.

Opposing hailstorm-specialist team.
Pre-cast buffs: Dustin's *Comfort of the Drenched Traveler*, Dagmar's *Wizard's Sidestep*, Éogan's ice-grip on the handholds.

**R2.** Opponents landed a *Pit of the Gaping Earth* directly under the cart — tipped backwards into a half-foot pit. Éogan made the Strength check on the ice grip and the wagon stayed intact.

Opponents signalled *Reign of Stones*; Dustin held a spontaneous *Rego Terram* concentration effect deflecting fist-sized stones to either side of the wagon. Éogan stood ready to fast-cast.
**Finish.** Sjórseiðr crossed the line. Hailstones poured down either side of the wagon without impact.
**Advance to Hastiludium semifinals.**

title: Dagmar wins Dimicatio Rounds 1 and 2 outright
notes: Two opponents in succession. Posing the Silent Question, mastered for quiet casting, both times sufficient. Neither opponent fast-cast a strong enough defense.
body_text:
Dagmar volunteered for the Dimicatio after a quick comparison of his InMe vs. Dustin's Arts.
**Round 1 — vs. Maga of Exspectatio (Ex Miscellanea).** Dagmar won initiative by a wide margin; cast *Posing the Silent Question* (loud voice, bold gesture, mastery for still/quiet bonus); rolled very high. Opponent fast-cast a defense — insufficient; her shoulders sagged before she finished. Judge called it.

title: Night market — show & tell, gambling, and the IOU settlements
notes: Animated toys, light shows, illusion myths, and accumulated IOUs changing hands between magi. Adam Smith loses ten gambling hands in a row and breaks bottles. Dagmar over-salts everything by old habit.
body_text:
After the close of the second day's events the field rolled over into an evening market — magi animating toys, casting light shows and illusions of old legends, and quietly **settling seven years of accumulated IOUs** between covenants.
Éogan, with a merchant's eye, took mental notes on which trinkets and effects could be commodified or replicated.
**Garrett Coffin** (grog) wandered the show sampling magical refreshments; failed his Stamina roll without Carousing and received a soft perceptual haze — "fairy lights, glamoured faces, a soft buzz." Found a sense of belonging among the assembled Hermetic community.
**Adam Smith** threw himself into dice against magi who could likely predict outcomes. After ten consecutive losses he kicked posts and smashed bottles.
**Dagmar** — life at sea has habituated him to salted food. He effused honest praise for the feast and over-salted everything regardless.

notes: Hilda places the two thesis copies. Fettelmid (Scarem Montem) gets the Latin copy with a Friday-deadline cursory appraisal. Juliana ex Bonisagus (Dragon's Rest) gets the Low German copy under protest; she wants the Latin and intends a full review back at Dragon's Rest.
body_text:

**Reviewer 1 — Fettelmid (Scarem Montem).** Approached Hilda first at the feast; given the **Latin** copy. Committed to a **cursory appraisal by end of day Friday (Day 3)**. Hilda plans to swing by the Scarem Montem tent on Friday to assess whether extended review is warranted.

Reluctantly accepted the **Low German** copy, but expects to **swap for the Latin** post-Tribunal. Plans to take the manuscript back to Dragon's Rest for thorough review — no timeline ("the time that it takes").
Hilda is strategising about leveraging the tradition of Hermetic hospitality to remain close to the manuscript at Dragon's Rest.

Timing is suspicious: a Bonisagus thesis from a Rhine-trained magus, then a turn toward another Rhine-connected figure with covenant-internal political weight.

title: Dagmar commissions a regio-navigation spell from Paulus ex Merinita
notes: After wandering the market and a brief conversation with a Mnemon of Tytalus from Lapis Crudus, Dagmar finds **Paulus ex Merinita** (Fudarus) — a specialist in faerie regio navigation. Two-component spell proposal; coordination via Redcaps.
body_text:
Dagmar browsed the tribunal market looking for tools for **time-orientation inside faerie regiones** — places where time flows unpredictably. Magic Theory roll: 8.
First contact: a **Mnemon of Tytalus** displaying materials from **Lapis Crudus** (itself trapped in a regio). Knowledgeable about regio levels but his wandering conversational style didn't yield a buy.
Among the displayed spell fragments Dagmar found one on **rarefication** — orienteering within faerie regiones — which led him to:
**Paulus ex Merinita (Fudarus).** A specialist in faerie regio navigation. Friendly, collaborative.
Paulus framed the problem with a current metaphor: inside a regio, temporal flows behave like currents in water. The proposed spell would give Dagmar agency over which current he swims in.
**Proposal — two components:**
1. A **ward effect** cast for a year on Dagmar's person — passive, always active.
2. When triggered by entering a faerie regio, the ward activates a **temporal-orientation effect** lasting one moon of external time (≈ half a moon inside an accelerated regio).
Paulus does not yet know how to build the triggered-ward component, but knows who to ask. He took Dagmar's contact info and will coordinate via the Redcaps.
Payment: vis types Sjórseiðr can supply. Final price and feasibility — TBD by post-Tribunal correspondence.

title: The Melee
date: Thursday, Tribunal Day 3 — afternoon through close
notes: Three grog champions (Garrett, Drest, Angus McPherson) take Spider's Palace in Round 1, Turris Vigilans in Round 2, and the whole melee outright at final placement — 1st place out of 24.
body_text:
Team Sjórseiðr in the Grog Melee:
• **Garrett** — offensive runner. Acrobatic, light on his feet.
• **Drest** — tackle/distraction. Good quickness; a blocker engaging defenders while Garrett ran the circles.
• **Angus McPherson** — newly created grog ("completely legitimate sailor"); home-circle defender. Foundry "tough guy" template.
**Pre-match diplomacy.** Angus rolled an excellent Presence check and brokered an alliance with **Semita Errabunda** (then transliterated "Samida Arabunda" at the table): "You go that way, we go that way. Hard here to make sure we honor our agreements."
**Round 1 — vs. Spider's Palace.**
Drest charged the Spider's Palace defender. The defender attempted to dodge and **botched** — definitely impeded.
Garrett executed a **baseball slide** through the magic circle, scraping the ring open with his momentum.
Spider's Palace eliminated first in the entire melee.
**Round 2 — vs. Turris Vigilans.**
Two defenders on Sjórseiðr's side this time.
• Drest charged forward as distraction again. **Attack roll: very high.**
• Angus's defense roll failed badly but he maintained his position at the home circle.
• Garrett sprinted around the engagement and made a **Stamina-based Athletics roll** to scrape out the Turris Vigilans circle with his club. Succeeded.
Turris Vigilans conceded gracefully — "not the sore loser type."
Session paused before final placement was calculated. GM tally noted: Sjórseiðr is confirmed **not in the bottom six** out of 24 teams.
**Final placement — 1st place out of 24.**
GM simmed the periphery and zoomed in once the ring shrank to roughly six teams.
**Angus** (very drunk by this point) used Charm (specialty: drunk) to lock his neighbouring team into a hold-the-line alliance — "second's a great place to be."
**Garrett** was teamed up on by all three Umbra Silvae grogs; he was freed when his grappler was pulled off-field as **Confluensis's** last man fell. He immediately charged to intercept a **Semita Errabunda** grog.
**Drest** rolled an explosive **38 on Athletics**, sprinted full-tilt, broke the opposing circle's centre, and overshot off the field.
**Angus**, oblivious to any host-favouring etiquette, calmly claimed the third undefended objective.
**Result: Sjórseiðr grogs — 1st place out of 24 teams.** Heavy side-betting from spectators who had not expected this.

title: Valdemar's joust Round 1 vs. Leonidas of Cunfin
notes: Pre-spells: Strike Swift and Sure (+3 init), Master of Magic Combat, Thurisaz on lance. Valdemar rolls 30; Leonidas botches defense. One pass.

One-pass victory. Leonidas was flung from the saddle into the crowd and caught by a spectator who bear-hugged the fall safe.

Valdemar's commentary afterward: "a magical bullshit lance is no substitute for actual jousting skill."

title: Valdemar's joust Round 2 vs. Mirna of Merinita
notes: Mirna rides a Dr. Seuss creature and splits into shadow copies. Two passes: Valdemar guesses the real one in P1, runs her down on Sleipnir-speed in P2.
body_text:
Added pre-spell for this match: **Swifter Than Any Horse** — the horse moves with the speed of Sleipnir's eight legs (+6 initiative). Combined initiative bonus ~+9.
**Opponent: Mirna of Merinita (Exspectatio).** Rides a Dr.-Seuss-like magical creature — mammalian, spindly legs, long neck, dandelion-shaped head. Runs more like a bear than a horse.
**Pass 1.** Mirna used *Wizard's Sidestep* plus additional phantasms — multiple shadow copies of herself. Valdemar guessed the **fourth** figure correctly and struck the true form. Mirna took a **light wound**, did not yield, called for best-of-three.
**Pass 2.** Swifter Than Any Horse active — the horse's legs blurred to invisibility. Valdemar closed in a heartbeat and struck cleanly (rolled 22). Mirna dropped her lance and conceded, bowing.
**Advances to joust semifinals.** Next opponent: Arx Argentea. Other semifinalists noted (subject to confirmation): Montverte, Scarem Montem, Oleron.

title: Wilhelm Stienauer ex Bonisagus arrives
notes: New PC introduction. Bonisagus research magus from Durenmar (Rhine Tribunal) with a seven-year folk-magic breakthrough thesis. Travels with brother, scribe Hilda, and two research assistants.
body_text:
**Wilhelm Stienauer** — Bonisagus research magus from the Rhine Tribunal. Trained at **Durenmar** under parens Agustus Rivaldi. Born 1197, gauntleted recently — 26 years old at arrival.
Life's work for seven years: an **original-research breakthrough on folk magic**, arguing that mundane hedge traditions (wise women, folk healers, weather-predictors, water-witches) constitute a distinct and previously undertheorized category whose mechanics can refine Hermetic theory.
Came to Normandy seeking peer reviewers and publication; expected a dry administrative meeting, was completely blindsided by the festival tournament atmosphere.
**Characteristics:** Int +3, Sta +2, Com +2, Per +1, Pre −2, Qik −2.
**Flaws:** Small Frame, Motion Sickness. **Virtues:** Minor Magical Focus (TBD), two others TBD.
**Art pillars:** Rego 17, Vim 16. **Equipment:** Amulet of Tongues. **House discrepancy on the sheet** (lists Bjornaer) — corrected in play to Bonisagus.
Entourage:
• **His brother** — mundane scholar from Cologne; the Low German thesis copy was originally for him.
• **Hilda** — Wilhelm's scribe, assistant, and publicist; organisational spine of the review process. Practical, no-nonsense.
• **Karl and one other research assistant** — field researchers who travel to study folk practitioners in situ. Both spectacularly drunk at the feast (bobbing for apples in wine).
Approached the covenant after the hastiludium. Got the crash course on Normandy's tournament-resource model; was theoretically captivated.
Éogan invited him to Hibernia for folk-magic fieldwork in a future season.
Wilhelm's **Rhine Tribunal Lore botch**: he knows nothing about the Lotharingian secession — Rhine separatists at the Tribunal may misread his ignorance as evasion or sympathy.

title: Hervé of Turris Vigilans's mutual-defense pact for Valdemar
notes: Hervé ex Tytalus offers a mutual-defense pact plus access to preserved texts on spontaneous magic. His intelligence about Valdemar is unsettlingly precise. He gives Valdemar a blue sash as the signal of accord.
body_text:
**Hervé ex Tytalus (Turris Vigilans)** approached Valdemar at the market.
**Offer.** A mutual-defense pact between Sjórseiðr and Turris Vigilans, plus access to Turris Vigilans's **preserved texts on spontaneous magic** — exactly the resource Valdemar's Diedne-line magic would benefit from most.
**The tell.** Hervé's intelligence was *unsettlingly* good — he knew exactly what to offer. It was **Valdemar**, not Rán, who was rattled by what Hervé knew. (Rán, asked later, judged him pleasant and honest but "he knew things about me he shouldn't have.")
Hervé handed Valdemar a **blue sash** to be worn as the signal of accord when Valdemar was ready to commit.

title: Llewellyn's time-crystal offer to Dagmar
notes: A Stonehenge free agent offers a quartz-on-a-chain "resonant with the platonic ideal of time" — a magical atomic clock for detecting time-dilation in regiones. Price: accompany him into a regio of Dagmar's choosing.
body_text:
**Llewellyn ex Miscellanea** (Stonehenge free agent) approached Dagmar at the night market.
**The item.** A quartz crystal on a chain — "resonant with the platonic ideal of time." Effectively a magical atomic clock for detecting time dilation in regiones — exactly complementing Dagmar's commission with Paulus.
**The price.** Accompany Llewellyn into a regio of Dagmar's choosing. Llewellyn insists, in defiance of most contemporary regio theory, that **all magical regiones are ultimately one**.
**The tell.** Dagmar's premonitions flagged that Llewellyn is himself **slightly out of sync with the world's time** — speech clipping at irregular intervals. He likely needs the crystal or an anti-aging ritual himself.
Dagmar expressed cautious interest. Nothing signed.

title: Scarem Montem steals the Tapestry and declares for Lotharingia
notes: Dawn was wrong — hushed magi, Montverte grogs cordoning buildings. The Tapestry (host's prize relic, central to the Norman Conquest staged event) was gone, and Scarem Montem with it. Scarem Montem then declared early for the Lotharingian tribunal — a vassal of Montverte defecting at the host's tribunal.
body_text:
Dawn on Day 4 was off. Magi conversations dropped to mutters; Montverte grogs ringed buildings; the central yard had the wrong sort of quiet.
**Scarem Montem stole the Tapestry** (the host's prize relic central to the Norman Conquest staged event) and fled overnight. Montverte **cancelled the Norman Conquest** outright and zeroed those points across the board.
**Scarem Montem then declared, openly, for the Lotharingian Tribunal** — well before the next Grand Tribunal, putting every covenant with secession sympathies on the spot. Scarem Montem was *Montverte's vassal*: a defection at the host's own tribunal.
Implication for the covenant: **Scarem Montem still held the Latin copy of Wilhelm's thesis**, taken under an honour-bound agreement to review and return.

title: Day 4 morning — the covenant huddle
notes: Four decisions land: compete to win the Hastiludium; Valdemar throws the joust against Hervé; Oleron's offer parked for reassessment; concern about appearing crypto-separatist if they finish too high. Valerian absent — did not return overnight.
body_text:
Pre-events on Day 4, the covenant huddled with the theft, the cancelled host event, and the three pending offers all on the table.
**Decision 1 — Hastiludium.** Compete to win Wilhelm's event; no offers attached.
**Decision 2 — Joust.** Valdemar will **throw the joust** against Hervé to seal the Turris Vigilans mutual-defense pact, doing so subtly — a missed angle, not an obvious dive.
**Decision 3 — Oleron.** Reconsider after standings settle; try to extract a favour or non-vassal alliance from Raoul instead of full vassalage.
**Decision 4 — Optics.** With Scarem Montem's defection still rippling through the field, finishing too high while remaining publicly independent risks the covenant being read as **crypto-separatist**. Calibrate accordingly.
**Valerian was absent.** He had not returned overnight.

title: Dimicatio semifinal vs. Raoul of Oleron — the won-anyway match
notes: Dagmar intends to throw the match by leading with his weakest spell. Raoul's opening Rego Vim does not penetrate; Dagmar's "weak" Pose the Silent Question lands repeatedly. Both leave the field dumbfounded.
body_text:
Dagmar greeted Raoul cordially, intending to throw the match — leading with **Pose the Silent Question**, his weakest viable opening — to give Oleron the win and leave the Oleron-vassalage door open as a favour.
Raoul's opening **Rego Vim** did not penetrate.
Dagmar's "weak" spell **landed anyway** — repeatedly. Raoul could not get a defense up.
Both magi left the field dumbfounded.
**Dagmar wins. Advances to the Dimicatio finals — against his explicit intention.**

title: Hastiludium semifinal vs. Iborus
notes: Lauda ex Jerbiton splits into nine illusory copies; Theodolph ex Tytalis casts Trust of Childlike Faith on Éogan. Éogan rolls 38, sees through everything, gains encounter-long immunity to Theodolph's mental magic. Sjórseiðr advances to the finals.
body_text:
**Opponents (Iborus):** Lauda ex Jerbiton (illusionist), Theodolph ex Tytalis (mentalist), plus a third caster — confirmation TBD.
**Opening.** Lauda split into **nine illusory copies** of herself. Theodolph cast **Trust of Childlike Faith** on Éogan, intended to soften him into compliance.
**Éogan rolled 38.** Saw through the illusions *and* the mental magic itself — and gained **immunity to Theodolph's mental magic for the rest of the encounter** as a consequence of the exceptional roll.
Dagmar (using *Eyes of the Eagle*) and Éogan together picked out the real Lauda. Éogan's torrent of water hit her cleanly; she **botched** her magic resistance and was blown clean off her wine cask.
**Sjórseiðr advances to the Hastiludium finals.**

title: Joust vs. Hervé — Valdemar tries to throw, Hervé botches first
notes: Valdemar flashes the blue sash and plans a last-moment deflection. Rosie squeals; Hervé's giant dog mount spooks and throws him before contact. Valdemar wins down an empty lane, dismounts to help him up, insists quietly that it wasn't him.
body_text:
Per the morning's decision, Valdemar entered the joust intending to **throw the match** against Hervé to seal the Turris Vigilans pact.
Hervé rode a **giant dog mount**. Valdemar flashed the **blue sash** in greeting — accord acknowledged.
Plan: deflect at the last moment, take the fall.
What actually happened: **Rosie squealed** at exactly the wrong moment. Hervé's dog spooked; Hervé **botched his ride roll** and was thrown. Another magus on the sidelines stunned the dog before it reached the crowd.
**Valdemar won down an empty lane.** The throw was wrecked through no fault of his own.
He dismounted to help Hervé up, and quietly insisted that **it wasn't him**.

  • What actually happened: Rosie squealed at exactly the wrong moment. Hervé's dog spooked; Hervé botched his ride roll and was thrown. Another magus on the sidelines stunned the dog before it reached the crowd.
  • Valdemar won down an empty lane. The throw was wrecked through no fault of his own.
  • He dismounted to help Hervé up, and quietly insisted that it wasn't him.

title: Valerian interrogates Wilhelm about the Brabant/Church conspiracy
date: Friday, Tribunal Day 4 (after both the dimicatio semifinal and final)
notes: Wilhelm assumed Valerian wanted to talk about his thesis; the real subject was a conspiracy involving the Duke of Brabant and the Church. Valerian closes with "I look forward to reading your thesis" — though he has not read it.
body_text:
While Dagmar's dimicatio semifinal ran on the field, **Valerian** approached **Wilhelm** out of view and began a low-key conversation.
Wilhelm, who knew Valerian had been associated with the thesis-review track via Hilda, assumed they were about to discuss the manuscript.
**The real subject:** a conspiracy involving the **Duke of Brabant and the Church**. Valerian's follow-up questions referenced people and topics Wilhelm hadn't yet mentioned, signalling that he already knew a great deal and was checking what Wilhelm knew or had let slip.
Valerian closed with "I look forward to reading your thesis" and vanished. **(Note: Valerian has not, in fact, read the thesis.)**
Wilhelm leaves the encounter knowing Valerian is dangerous without knowing the direction.

title: The fleet's trade income while the covenant was away at the Tribunal
notes: While the magi competed at the Tribunal, the covenant's three ships kept trading. Éogan's standing orders kept the Brineborn conservative; the Scholar's Wake, left to Heynric's judgment, swung bigger and it paid off.
body_text:
With the magi occupied at Montverte, the covenant's ships carried on trading independently, each captain/crew making their own risk call.
**Brineborn** — Éogan had left standing orders not to take risks in his absence. Low risk, low reward: netted **11 mythic pounds**. Confirmed the right call — the higher-risk play would have returned nothing this round.
**Tide of Memory** — also played conservative, for a similarly modest but positive result.
**The Scholar's Wake** — Dustin let Heynric the Merchant make the call. Heynric let it ride, cleared the bottom rung of risk, and came back with the best haul: **15 mythic pounds**.
**Total: 35 mythic pounds richer**, collectively, on top of whatever the Tribunal itself paid out.

title: Wilhelm's manuscript reveals a Divine-vis wrinkle
notes: Rereading his own folk-magic thesis, Wilhelm clocks that once a magic-theory guideline exists for a phenomenon, its basic lab-activity benefits open up to anyone — including vis harvesting inside holy auras. Which means spells cast with that vis become, technically, Implements of the Divine.
body_text:
With a day or two of downtime before the last finals, Wilhelm went back over his own manuscript more carefully than he had in weeks.
The catch: per the standard Hermetic rule that developing a magic-theory guideline unlocks the **basic benefits of laboratory activities** for anyone using it, and Wilhelm's folk-magic system covers all four Techniques/Forms-equivalent phenomena — the implication is that mundanes trained through his system could **harvest vis**, including from **holy (Divine) auras**, not merely fae or magical ones.
The wrinkle: magic built from Divine vis apparently becomes, by the working theory at the table, an **Implement of the Divine** — not corrupted or penalized, just now legally/theologically "God's," implicitly, the way a company logo becomes a stakeholder's the moment it appears in a film. No botch penalty attached, but a real second-order consequence for anyone drawing on it.
Wilhelm's gallows-humor read on the Church angle: if anyone in Rome ever actually reads the thesis rather than reacting to rumors of it, their most likely response is a startled, genuine thank-you.

title: Dietrich pitches folk magic to scholars and a Redcap; Dustin interrogates him
notes: Wilhelm's brother Dietrich — a Cologne cathedral-school professor with a rhetorician's Presence — works a tavern crowd of mundane scholars and a Redcap. Dustin needles him hard on the Divine-vis danger; Dietrich extends Parma Magica for a proper scholastic debate rather than back down. Éogan and Dagmar eavesdrop with opposite reactions. [Rules note: the Boundary/Year spontaneous-casting capability described here is a feature of Wilhelm's non-Hermetic folk-magic system breaking Hermetic limits; it does not alter core Hermetic magic, where the Boundary target forces a Ritual and cannot be cast spontaneously — see open-questions tl026.]
body_text:
**Dietrich** (Wilhelm's brother — professor of medicine and philosophy at a Cologne cathedral school, more at home teaching in a tavern's back room than a formal hall) held forth to a knot of mundane scholars and at least one Redcap, evangelizing his brother's folk-magic thesis.
His pitch, in the confident, theatrical register of a man used to lecturing: mundanes can do "basic magic" once the system is taught — season-long lab work, a few pounds of vis, eventually casting on their own — and the system appears to work equally well in Divine auras ("align your magic with the will of God"), a claim he leans on hard rhetorically.
**Dustin listened in but pushed back sharply**, especially on the vis-from-holy-auras point ("wait, that's dangerous"). Dietrich's answer: no more dangerous than fae vis, just with its own side effects — and he clearly felt Dustin's Gift as an unpleasant edge to the conversation, gritted through it, then formally offered to have **Parma Magica extended** over him so they could debate as scholars instead. Dustin agreed; **no botch** on the roll.
Under structured debate, Dietrich laid out the three ways to learn a new Hermetic guideline — experimentation, being taught via initiation, or **integrating someone else's prior understanding of it** — and used Wilhelm as the live example: Wilhelm was taught actual folk **dowsing/"folk banding"** as a child, before his Gift opened, and that knowledge survived the Opening intact. That's the seed the whole thesis grew from.
The system's theorized reason for being so **syncretic** (working across pagan, fae, and Divine contexts alike): unlike Hermetic magic, it doesn't call on "gods of magic" or power names at all — it calls on **humanity's own innate relationship to nature**. Dietrich's framing: everyone with the Gift has magical "perfect pitch"; this system argues *everyone* — Gifted or not — has *rhythm*. Someone at the table called it a **proto-Spinozist magic system**.
Dietrich also aired the thesis's acknowledged problems: success would mean **thousands of new folk-magic practitioners** wanting into a Rhine/Normandy magical economy sized for a much smaller Order — a real resource and wild-vis strain — plus the obvious Church-scrutiny risk. He name-drops one cautionary case his researchers turned up: someone practicing what looked like infernal magic (commanding reality directly — "you will do this for me") who turned out not to be invoking anything demonic at all, just committing the sin of pride. His answer to Church risk, delivered as pure rhetorical bravado: send *him* their scholars, he'll happily walk them through it.
One concrete new mechanical thread surfaced: folk-magic guidelines can apparently support **spontaneous casting at Boundary and Year durations**, targets/durations normally locked to formal ritual infrastructure. Flagged as something **Valdemar** — already pulling at spontaneous-magic threads — would find very interesting, though he's keeping that interest close to the chest for now.
**Éogan and Dagmar eavesdropped from the side.** Éogan recalled a person or two from his own village who could do small folk-magic-flavored things (calming/calling animals) without ever being identified as Gifted, and mused that formalizing hedge traditions into Hermetic theory could help magi be seen as less of pariahs among mundanes. Dagmar stayed openly unconvinced by the showmanship of the pitch — not the substance, just the hard sell — and was characteristically blunt that he hopes someone else does the actual integration work; his own priority remains keeping the covenant solvent.

Under structured debate, Dietrich laid out the three ways to learn a new Hermetic guideline — experimentation, being taught via initiation, or integrating someone else's prior understanding of it — and used Wilhelm as the live example: Wilhelm was taught actual folk dowsing/"folk banding" as a child, before his Gift opened, and that knowledge survived the Opening intact. That's the seed the whole thesis grew from.

The system's theorized reason for being so syncretic (working across pagan, fae, and Divine contexts alike): unlike Hermetic magic, it doesn't call on "gods of magic" or power names at all — it calls on humanity's own innate relationship to nature. Dietrich's framing: everyone with the Gift has magical "perfect pitch"; this system argues everyone — Gifted or not — has rhythm. Someone at the table called it a proto-Spinozist magic system.

Dietrich also aired the thesis's acknowledged problems: success would mean thousands of new folk-magic practitioners wanting into a Rhine/Normandy magical economy sized for a much smaller Order — a real resource and wild-vis strain — plus the obvious Church-scrutiny risk. He name-drops one cautionary case his researchers turned up: someone practicing what looked like infernal magic (commanding reality directly — "you will do this for me") who turned out not to be invoking anything demonic at all, just committing the sin of pride. His answer to Church risk, delivered as pure rhetorical bravado: send him their scholars, he'll happily walk them through it.

One concrete new mechanical thread surfaced: folk-magic guidelines can apparently support spontaneous casting at Boundary and Year durations, targets/durations normally locked to formal ritual infrastructure. Flagged as something Valdemar — already pulling at spontaneous-magic threads — would find very interesting, though he's keeping that interest close to the chest for now.

Éogan and Dagmar eavesdropped from the side. Éogan recalled a person or two from his own village who could do small folk-magic-flavored things (calming/calling animals) without ever being identified as Gifted, and mused that formalizing hedge traditions into Hermetic theory could help magi be seen as less of pariahs among mundanes. Dagmar stayed openly unconvinced by the showmanship of the pitch — not the substance, just the hard sell — and was characteristically blunt that he hopes someone else does the actual integration work; his own priority remains keeping the covenant solvent.

title: Wilhelm pitches Éogan on hedge-magic sea/weather traditions for the thesis
notes: Wilhelm's working theory is that Hermetic guidelines are mechanically universal, so finding hedge-magic equivalents (storm prediction, current-finding) anywhere would support the thesis. Éogan's own home tradition turns out to be water-finding rather than sea-current work, and runs close to Diedne-adjacent "Seekers" fieldwork methodology.
body_text:
Wilhelm's next concrete step for the thesis: find **weather-prediction or current-navigation** hedge traditions to demonstrate the system generalizes to a sea-faring context, not just land-bound folk practice.
His reasoning (per his working theory that **Hermetic guidelines are effectively universal targets** in game terms): a hedge tradition anywhere that reliably finds ocean currents or predicts storms would independently validate his thesis, regardless of who practices it.
**Éogan's read from experience:** for a sea covenant, control over wind and current isn't just survival — it's propulsion. He's personally more water- than air-inclined. But his own home tradition, as he understands it, wasn't actually a sea-navigation practice — it was oriented toward **finding fresh water inland/underground** for villages, and is more commonly associated with **fae magic** than open-ocean work.
Éogan noted his tradition survived mostly as an unbroken master-to-student thread ("a Hermetic cell in and of itself") rather than a documented body of theory, and that its more active practitioners run in the methodology of House Diedne's **Seekers** suborder — fieldwork his own research assistants use without having formally joined the Seekers themselves.
Open thread: Wilhelm still needs an actual example of hedge-magic sea-current-finding or storm-prediction to close the thesis's weakest citation gap; dowsing-for-water is closer to confirmed but doesn't fully prove the maritime case.

title: Dagmar and Dustin pitch Bertrand ex Verditius on storing the covenant's prizes
notes: With prize books and texts about to become a shipboard liability, Dagmar and Dustin pitch Confluensis (spelled "Confluences" in this session's transcript — same liege covenant as in prior sessions) on custodianship, not vassalage. Bertrand ex Verditius negotiates in person; a Bargain roll closes the terms, contingent on him checking with the covenant's inner circle before the finals end.
body_text:
Anticipating a haul of prize books and texts too valuable to risk at sea, Dagmar and Dustin sought out **Confluensis** at their tents to propose safekeeping — explicitly *not* vassalage, just custodianship with guaranteed access.
Met **Bertrand ex Verditius** — visually a man in his 50s who is, in fact, closer to 70 or 80; tanned, Mediterranean coloring; a big, bushy black beard. Bertrand needled Dagmar good-naturedly about a sea-covenant producing "such fine specimens."
**The pitch:** Confluensis holds any prize books/texts on Sjórseiðr's behalf; Sjórseiðr keeps full access and visits to work on them as needed; no formal vassalage, just a standing mutual arrangement.
**Dagmar rolled Area Lore: Normandy Tribunal** (stress die, +3 for prior tribunal research), got an **11**, and learned Confluensis is **significantly underperforming this Tribunal relative to its usual standing** — a covenant that pools and redistributes vassal winnings, meaning a bad Confluensis showing hurts its vassals too, and they're currently short on the usual leverage that comes with hosting a favor like this.
**Payment discussion:** the standard rate for a season of a magus's lab service is roughly **2–3 pawns of vis**. Bertrand fished for what else Sjórseiðr could offer instead — and, after a pointed once-over of Dagmar, asked outright whether **cross-border courier/smuggling work** was something they'd done before. Dagmar demurred; Dustin didn't — the covenant had, in fact, run exactly this kind of job already (the covert Creo Vis run for Montverte, kept off the Redcap network at Montverte's insistence).
**Dustin led the Bargain roll** (Communication, +3 assist from Dagmar) — **no botch**. Closing pitch: a season of general service is fine; being treated as someone's subordinate is not.
Bertrand agreed to take the offer back to Confluensis's inner circle (roughly 10–11 active magi at their home covenant; only a small contingent present at the Tribunal) and promised an answer **before the finals concluded**.

body_text:
Valdemar returned from his bracket having won cleanly against an early opponent and then against a **Semita Errabunda** rider, putting him in the **joust final against Montverte**, tied for first overall.
**Covenant debate:** finishing above a hosting leash-covenant risks the kind of resentment already visible from Confluensis; some at the table favored letting Montverte have it as a courtesy. Consensus landed on **going for the win regardless** — "let the chips fall where they may."

title: Dagmar's dimicatio final — a clean win, then a mirror-match loss to Caris of Oleron
notes: Two-match final. Dagmar means to win outright against a Tytalus opponent (name garbled in the recording) and go easy on Oleron's finalist as a diplomatic courtesy — but the second match, against a Criamon built by the GM as a deliberate mirror of Dagmar's own sheet, turns into a real, hard-fought loss.
body_text:
Dagmar entered the dimicatio final needing to beat two opponents: a **Tytalus magus** first (name unclear in the recording — heard as something close to "Quaerus"), and **Oleron's finalist** second. Going in, Dagmar planned to fight the first for real and **deliberately lose initiative** against Oleron's man as a diplomatic gesture.
**Match 1 — vs. the Tytalus magus.** Dagmar cast **Posing the Silent Question** (Intellego Mentem) again; the opponent fast-cast **Banish the Thought** as a defense, but it backfired — trying to force the intrusive thought out only reinforced it. His shoulders dropped and the match was called for Dagmar. He left the field abruptly, cordial but clearly rattled.
**Match 2 — vs. Caris ex Criamon (Oleron's finalist).** The GM built Caris explicitly as a **mirror of Dagmar's own character sheet** — boyish-faced, younger-looking than his real age, mild and a little blithe in manner.
Caris held his action, then opened with **Pierce the Magical Veil** — attempting to open a regio *on top of his opponent* mid-duel, an unusual and unsettling approach. Followed by **Past Lives**, an eerie effect suggesting the caster's mind holds conversations with great minds of the past (compared at the table to Dante and Virgil), aimed at Dagmar. Dagmar improvised a spontaneous **Intellego/Rego Mentem** defense — grounding himself in "the here, the now, it's me" — and it held (a **personal/momentary/individual** spontaneous effect against a −10 casting-score penalty, needing to clear roughly half the target level).
Caris pressed with **Words of the Unbroken Silence**, trying to plant a message directly in Dagmar's mind — blocked. He then switched tactics entirely and cast **Break the Shield**, a Perdo Vim effect functionally equivalent to dispelling Parma Magica — **Wizard's-War-tier stuff for a tournament match.** It landed. Dagmar described the sensation as the magical equivalent of being about to be disrobed and then not quite. His own spontaneous **Rego Vim** effort to restabilize his Parma (needing 9+, effectively against a −16 penalty) came up **one short**.
**Caris did not follow up.** Dagmar conceded, badly shaken but gracious; Caris, equally gracious: *"You will be delightful competition next tribunal. I look forward to seeing you there."*
**Result: Dagmar/Sjórseiðr places 2nd in the dimicatio** — a real loss to a genuinely tough opponent, not the soft diplomatic throw originally planned, though the outcome (a loss to Oleron) lines up with what Dagmar intended going in.

title: Hastiludium final vs. Lapis Crudus — first place
notes: Lapis Crudus — the recently-freed, 80-year-faerie-imprisoned independent — plays it destructive: fire, a pit trap, and a closing ball of abysmal flame that actually catches the wagon. Grip of Ice and a strong Unseen Porter carry Sjórseiðr across first, unburned. The GM also reveals an earlier bracket round was resolved off-screen in Sjórseiðr's favor to save table time — the covenant wins the Hastiludium outright.
body_text:
Opponent: **Lapis Crudus**, the independent covenant recently freed after an 80-year faerie imprisonment, fielding a "premier" Flambeau plus Tremere/Flambeau support (exact roster uncertain even to the GM in the moment). Reputation: destructive and "rollicking" — willing to injure a competitor's mount or rig rather than lose. Riding an enchanted **anvil** in place of a wagon.
Pre-cast as usual: Wizard's Sidestep, Grip of Ice, and a strong **Unseen Porter** pull (an exceptional roll — noticeably "buffer" than the wagon's usual pull).
**Opening.** A pillar of flame appears directly in the wagon's path; Éogan fast-casts a −5-penalized **Mighty Torrent of Water**, rolls **29**, douses it clean.
Dustin lands **Pillum of Fire** on Lapis Crudus's anvil, heating it forge-orange — countered when their caster **Soothes the Raging Flames** right back down.
Lapis Crudus opens **Pit of the Gaping Earth** in the wagon's path; the Unseen Porter routes around it, costing a little time but avoiding the hazard entirely.
Dustin tries **Broom of the Winds** on their rider to knock them loose; they pivot into **Circling Winds of Protection** instead — deflecting the attack, though it also denies them a wind-assisted speed boost.
**Closing move.** Lapis Crudus throws a **Ball of Abysmal Flame** at the wagon. A fast-cast **Creo Aquam** counter (classic counter-magic, matching totals) fails to beat their casting roll; a follow-up spontaneous dousing effect (needing 23+) rolls only **16** and also falls short — the fire catches.
Rather than break off this late in the race, the crew **rides it out**: a Stamina roll holds up, **Grip of Ice**'s literal ice cushions the burn (the grip loosens as it melts, faces get scorched, nothing worse), and one hand quenches the flame while the other holds the line.
The Unseen Porter's speed edge (**+4 net** relative to the opponents) carries Sjórseiðr across the line first — **no injuries**, thanks to the ice.
**GM note:** an earlier hastiludium bracket round the table didn't have time to play out live was resolved off-screen in Sjórseiðr's favor between sessions, to avoid pushing the tournament into a further session.
**Result: Sjórseiðr wins the Hastiludium outright — 1st place.**

title: Tribunal final standings: Sjórseiðr takes first overall, Confluensis takes the "Siege of Shame"
notes: Full placements read aloud at the closing feast. Confluensis's 13th-place finish ("the Siege of Shame," traditionally zero reward per a historical cheating scandal) directly explains the cold reception Dagmar gets minutes later. Sjórseiðr finishes 1st overall with 51 points and 31 pawns of vis.
body_text:
As the Redcaps tallied results, the closing feast doubled as the standings ceremony. Placements as announced (covenant names/ordinal titles as heard — a few uncertain):
  • **21st — the "Siege of Alms"** → **Florum** (a leash covenant), 12 pawns instead of zero.
  • **13th — the "Siege of Shame"** → **Confluensis** — **zero pawns**. There's Tribunal-wide lore behind the 13th-place designation, tied to a historical cheating scandal; landing there is a real public humiliation, not just a bad finish.
  • **7th — the "Siege of Notatus"** → **Fudarus**, 17 pawns. (Siege name confirmed against the tribunal workbook's prize-rank table, not the recording itself, which was unclear here.)
  • **4th — Montverte**, 15 pawns.
  • **3rd — Merces Aurea**, 30 points.
  • **2nd — the "Siege of Valor"** → **Oleron**, 31 points.
  • **1st — "The Siege of Normandy"** → **Sjórseiðr**, with a total of **51 points and a reward of 31 pawns of vis** — the second-place gap was 31 to 51, meaning the Hastiludium win alone pulled the covenant well clear of the tie.
A representative from each covenant was called forward in order to draft prizes.

title: Bertrand denies the book-storage arrangement ever happened
notes: Fresh off the Siege of Shame, Bertrand flatly denies the morning's negotiation ever happened, then turns back to his meal. The book-storage question is back open — Fudarus or Oleron are the live alternatives, with Oleron the more promising given how Raoul's conversation goes minutes later.
body_text:
Confluensis never followed up with terms before the finals ended, as promised. Dagmar sought out **Bertrand ex Verditius** directly at the feast to close the loop.
Bertrand's response, cold and immediate: **"I know of no arrangement."** He turned back to his food without another word.
Dagmar's read leaving the conversation: Confluensis is not housing the books. Given the timing — this lands minutes after Confluensis's public **13th-place humiliation** — the snub reads less like forgetfulness and more like wounded pride refusing to be seen doing a favor for the covenant that just helped bury them.
**Open thread:** the covenant's prize texts still need a custodian. Fudarus (closer, but Dagmar's openly not fond of Tytalus magi) and Oleron (further, but visibly warmer toward Sjórseiðr as of this same feast) are the two live options.

title: Éogan smooths things over with Raoul of Oleron
notes: Éogan apologizes for the covenant's matches not going Oleron's way as intended. Raoul waves it off — genuinely delighted that Sjórseiðr's rise embarrassed Confluensis and Montverte — and starts treating the covenant as a peer, floating a favorable resource swap.
body_text:
Éogan sought out **Raoul of Oleron** after the standings to apologize — the covenant had hoped the finals would go Oleron's way as a courtesy, but between real opposition and events moving faster than planned, that didn't fully happen.
Raoul brushed it off immediately, in good humor, and pulled Éogan down for a drink instead: as far as he's concerned, Sjórseiðr beating **Confluensis and Montverte** — old rivals of Oleron's within the tribunal's leash-covenant politics — is a win worth celebrating regardless of who beat whom in the bracket.
**Reading of the room:** Raoul now treats Sjórseiðr as something close to a peer rather than a prospective vassal — "between the two of us, we're running away with it" — and is open to working together where interests align.
**Concrete offer:** Oleron has additional easily-reachable island/coastal resources not on the official prize list that Raoul is willing to trade flexibly for something more inland, further south — convenient if the covenant ends up routing through Oleron territory anyway (e.g. to store Wilhelm's books there instead of Confluensis).

title: Dietrich warns Wilhelm about the company he's keeping
notes: Wilhelm is still processing the covenant's win as a cheerful, low-stakes camp-games victory. Dietrich, working purely off tavern chatter and not the covenant's actual politics, still reads the room correctly enough to pull his brother aside.
body_text:
As the covenant's win rippled through the feast, Wilhelm's read on the whole tournament stayed resolutely innocent: to him it landed somewhere between a summer-camp relay race and being crowned king-for-a-day at a village fair — fun, a little silly, not obviously dangerous.
A nearby onlooker (heard as **Helga**) pointedly noted that a lot of covenants seem awfully sore about losing what's ostensibly just a game — more than mere competitive pride, it's described as **a reaffirming of the order of things**, one Sjórseiðr just upended by winning fair and square, with very material seven-year consequences attached (first pick of the tribunal's rare texts and resources).
**Dietrich**, without knowing any of the covenant's actual political entanglements, picked up enough from the ambient chatter to pull Wilhelm aside privately: *"Brother. I think you should be mindful about how deeply you throw your lot in with them. I believe they have made some enemies."* He then stepped back to let Wilhelm keep his privacy with the rest of the table.
Wilhelm, still mentally filing the win as a harmless game, didn't take the warning especially seriously — his more pressing concern stayed retrieving his stolen Latin manuscript and getting to Ireland.
body_html:
As the covenant's win rippled through the feast, Wilhelm's read on the whole tournament stayed resolutely innocent: to him it landed somewhere between a summer-camp relay race and being crowned king-for-a-day at a village fair — fun, a little silly, not obviously dangerous.

A nearby onlooker (heard as Helga) pointedly noted that a lot of covenants seem awfully sore about losing what's ostensibly just a game — more than mere competitive pride, it's described as a reaffirming of the order of things, one Sjórseiðr just upended by winning fair and square, with very material seven-year consequences attached (first pick of the tribunal's rare texts and resources).

Dietrich, without knowing any of the covenant's actual political entanglements, picked up enough from the ambient chatter to pull Wilhelm aside privately: "Brother. I think you should be mindful about how deeply you throw your lot in with them. I believe they have made some enemies." He then stepped back to let Wilhelm keep his privacy with the rest of the table.

Wilhelm, still mentally filing the win as a harmless game, didn't take the warning especially seriously — his more pressing concern stayed retrieving his stolen Latin manuscript and getting to Ireland.

title: Post-Tribunal reflections: Dagmar's paranoia, Dustin's fame, and a wood sliver from every prize
notes: The table's go-around on how each PC is processing an unplanned #1 finish. Dagmar is deep in a paranoia spiral about what winning "for real" now exposes the covenant to, and starts covertly marking every prize item in case something is swapped or stolen later. Dustin is just thrilled to be famous. Éogan also uses the departure to finally share the private Lotharingian pitch Bridget of Scarem Montem had made him on the free day (see open-questions t010).
body_text:
**Dagmar** came out of the Tribunal shell-shocked rather than triumphant — the plan had been to lay low, and instead the covenant is now the most visible independent in Normandy. He's replaying how the lay-low/throw-the-match plans went "horribly, horribly wrong" and is settling into a genuinely paranoid stretch: watching for anyone paying the covenant too much attention, and bracing for **Solving** (his long-vanished parens) to reappear and have opinions about all of it — table joke: "he just went out for milk, he'll be back any day now."
**Concrete paranoia measure:** for every book, scroll, or other prize item the covenant receives from the Tribunal, Dagmar takes a **tiny sliver from it** to keep on his person — insurance so that if something underhanded happens later (a swap, a theft, tampering) he has a physical/arcane link to try to trace it back.
**Dustin**, by contrast, is delighted. He reads the win as unambiguously good for his personal legacy and renown, even if the *kind* of fame it brings (a jumped-up sea-covenant embarrassing three leash covenants at their own tournament) isn't necessarily the flattering kind. Table comparison: reputation as faction-specific currency — Order-of-Hermes fame doesn't automatically convert to goodwill with covenants that just got shown up.
**Éogan**, as the covenant made ready to sail, finally surfaced a card he'd been holding since the free day: on the quiet, **Bridget of Scarem Montem** (House Tremere) had pulled him aside under an obscuring spell and walked him through the **Lotharingian secession** case, offering to hold his Tourney winnings in jurisdictions beyond Normandy's recall. He'd sat on it through the games — but with Scarem Montem having since stolen the host's Tapestry and openly declared for the Lotharingian Tribunal, the private courtship read very differently in hindsight, and he laid the whole thing out for the covenant on the way out.

title: Stijntje's first taste of peers — and of how different she is from them
notes: Stijntje's real takeaway from the Tribunal wasn't the tournament — it was meeting other apprentices for the first time and discovering how little she has in common with them beyond the mechanics of being gauntleted.
body_text:
For **Stijntje**, the standout experience of the Tribunal wasn't the tournament at all — it was simply having **peers for the first time**: other apprentices her own age and status, something her isolated upbringing on a ship-based covenant never afforded her.
That contact cut both ways. Meeting them made it obvious how different her situation is: she no longer has to actively pass as male in every context now that other apprentices clock the gender gap in the room; she is visibly **more affluent and educated** than most of the other apprentices, who mostly went straight from whatever village they were discovered in to a stationary covenant; and she has simply **seen more of the world** than any of them, most of whom haven't gone much of anywhere. Table comparison: something like growing up on a cruise ship.
Likely friction: her nobility and evident worldliness read to the other apprentices as gloating even when it isn't meant that way — the classic "you haven't been to Cancún" dynamic, just transposed into Hermetic apprenticeship.
Underscored again in this conversation: she did **run away from home** for reasons still unstated, and back home she has to fight the covenant's pig for bed space — her situation isn't as charmed as the other apprentices might assume from her manner.

title: The covenant turns a corner: breakeven, trade economics, and an eye on jurisdictional arbitrage
notes: First real financial good news for the covenant: they broke even last year (not counting loan repayment), and with the Tribunal's hard assets in hand, profitability is now "fairly trivial" if they want it. Extended discussion of the Rule of Silver, magically-produced trade goods, and long-range multi-tribunal trade routes.
body_text:
**State of the covenant's finances, per the GM:** the covenant **broke even last year** — costs did not exceed revenue, though that figure doesn't yet include any loan repayment. With the Tribunal's prize assets now in hand (on top of the Duke's existing payments), the covenant is past its early hard-scrabble years; **real profitability is now trivial to reach** if the party chooses to prioritize it. Not destitute any longer "unless it is your choice or a great failure."
**The Rule of Silver:** a magus may create at most **2 lbs of silver-value goods per Tribunal per year** without inviting real scrutiny — enforcement varies enormously by Tribunal (some care only if the goods are magical weapons; the Rhine Tribunal cares if magic touched the goods or their transport *at all*). Salt (desalinated seawater, reduced to solid) is the easiest magically-produced trade good; explicitly discussed as "legit trade" even though magically created, so long as it's kept under the radar per-Tribunal.
**Jurisdictional arbitrage:** with ~5-6 Tribunals reasonably reachable by ship (Rhine, Normandy, Stonehenge, Hibernia, plus further effort to reach Novgorod), the covenant could legally clear roughly **60-100 lbs of silver a year** just by distributing sales across multiple Tribunals' individual limits — a genuine, legal income stream, separate from anything shadier.
**Infrastructure idea (not yet committed):** an enchanted **stone cargo-sled** — a two-ton, four-ton-loaded flying platform, ~Level 20 enchantment, ~45 mph, functionally a magical helicopter for hauling trade goods (and echoing the departed PC **Kor Ex Flambeau**'s unfinished, much larger version of the same idea, last seen unfinished somewhere out in the world).
**Attitude check:** the table explicitly flagged that each PC sits differently on a "how much do I care about the rules" scale for magically-tinged trade — Dagmar didn't care until the Tribunal made clear people *will* make an example of the covenant if caught, and has shifted hard toward caution as a result.
