title: The Hound of Cassel: a stolen Scarem Montem hull — risk and opportunity
notes: While planning Wilhelm's return trip to Scarem Montem for his stolen manuscript, the table half-remembers that the ship they'd send him on was itself taken from Scarem Montem at some point in the covenant's past. Floated as either a bargaining chip (ship for book) or a very awkward thing to show up in.
body_text:
While planning how Wilhelm returns to **Scarem Montem** to retrieve his stolen Latin thesis copy, the table pinned down a live asset: the covenant holds the **Hound of Cassel** — the very hull it pirated from Scarem Montem — currently berthed at the covenant's **Isle of Man** base and available for use. That provenance cuts both ways; it's **both a risk and an opportunity**:
**Opportunity — a bargaining chip.** The covenant can offer to hand the *Hound of Cassel* back to Scarem Montem in exchange for Wilhelm's manuscript — a clean ship-for-book swap that gives both sides what they want and defuses the theft.
**Risk — the same hull is evidence.** Wilhelm must not sail into Scarem Montem aboard their own stolen ship to ask for his book back; arriving in the *Hound of Cassel* announces the piracy before a word is spoken. (Dark-comedy option floated: keep Wilhelm — who doesn't know the ship is stolen — in the dark, and pass it off as *"a legally distinct ship, note the different name painted right over the old one."*)
The "rough justice" framing — fair's fair, they took the book, the covenant keeps the ship — was also floated, but the swap-for-swap is the stronger play when Wilhelm goes back in 1224.

title: Éogan buys jade for a future Talisman; Dagmar eyes a longevity ritual; Dustin catches up on his own Arts
notes: Three separate long-horizon character projects declared in the same conversation.
body_text:
**Éogan** picked up **jade** (preferred over plain crystal — house-ruled as +Aquam) at the Tribunal markets, with an eye toward beginning work on a **Talisman** — his reasoning: a magus doesn't need to be especially powerful to start one, and the earlier it's begun the more useful it becomes over time.
**Dagmar** is starting to plan toward a **longevity ritual**, aware the covenant's magi are getting into their late twenties. He's deliberately **not** rushing it — real aging doesn't set in until around 35, and he wants his **Creo** significantly stronger before he attempts the ritual, so he's treating this as prep work for "next year or so" rather than an immediate project. (Noted in passing: longevity rituals also cause infertility — a real cost, not just a delay.)
**Dustin** admits to having **neglected his own Arts study** recently between running trade and teaching Stijntje, and is planning to make time to catch up on both fronts going forward.

title: Éogan's Connacht backstory, laid bare
notes: In the course of planning the Ireland trip, Éogan's player laid out his full backstory for the first time: a hedge-magic hostage exchange, an ex-Miscellanea dowsing parens, and a covenant called Vigil at the top of the map.
body_text:
Éogan is originally from **Connacht** (heard on tape as "conduct") — the region of Ireland the transcript describes as *not* under Hermetic control, where hedge magi "made their last stand." A standing treaty between the Hibernia Tribunal and Connacht's hedge tradition requires Connacht to hand over **seven Gifted individuals per Tribunal cycle**; Éogan was one of the seven traded over as a child.
He was apprenticed not to a hedge magus but to a Hermetic one — **an ex-Miscellanea magus, one of the last of a line of "dowsing wizards"** (the water-finding tradition Éogan referenced back at the Tribunal itself). His upbringing was mostly **wandering between magic sites**, learning directly from the source rather than from formal instruction, with the covenant **Vigil** (marked at the far north of the Hibernia map) as the place he returned to for what formal book-learning he did get.

title: Dagmar's winter at Oleron: the books, the rival-turned-acquaintance, and a crash course in Tribunal politics
notes: With Confluensis having reneged, Oleron becomes the actual custodian of the covenant's tournament-prize books — and Dagmar decides to winter there in person rather than just visiting for a season, for three separate reasons.
body_text:
The covenant's tournament-prize books and texts are going to **Oleron** — the book-storage question left open when Bertrand ex Verditius denied any arrangement (see the earlier Tribunal-week entries) resolves here, quietly, in Oleron's favor, consistent with how warmly Raoul had already been treating the covenant.
**Dagmar will winter at Oleron in person**, not just spend a working season there, with three stated goals: (1) actually use/study the prize texts on-site, (2) spend time with **Caris ex Criamon**, the magus he faced in the Dimicatio final — a fellow Criamon who, by his own account, hasn't been among his own order in a very long time, and (3) get properly briefed on the Tribunal politics the covenant has just stepped into, which he admits he still doesn't fully understand.
His ship will return for him come **spring 1224**.
Dagmar's wintering there in person also serves as the covenant's **formal acknowledgment** of the (non-vassal, protector/patron-flavored) relationship with Oleron — no separate representative needed — and he offered the covenant's trade/commerce capacity as a thank-you gesture.
**Winter reading plan at Oleron:** Dagmar splits two seasons of study — **The Babble Within Thought** in Fall, and a personal loan from **Caris** (his old Dimicatio-final rival, now something like a mentor-in-residence at Oleron) in Winter.

title: Season plans: Ireland, the Isle of Man, and a covenant full of quiet magic items
notes: Travel and season assignments locked in for the trip home. Running gag: Wilhelm's been sitting on a bottomless grain dish for weeks without mentioning it.
body_text:
**Travel.** The **Brineborn** (Éogan's ship) carries Éogan, Wilhelm, Hilda, and one research assistant north toward **Dragon's Rest**, then **Scarem Montem** (to retrieve Wilhelm's stolen Latin thesis copy), then on to **Ireland** for Wilhelm's promised folk-magic fieldwork. Separately, **Valerian**, aboard the **Adamant**, ferries **Dietrich**, Hilda's remaining research assistant, and Wilhelm's other assistant toward a rendezvous at Dragon's Rest.
**Wintering.** See [053_2026-06-20_ireland-travel-plan-finalized] for the full plan — the covenant winters near Carrick, Ireland, with the Isle of Man as a waypoint stop.
**Autumn season assignments:**
  • **Dagmar** — heading to Oleron with the covenant's prize books; see the dedicated session-7 entry for the expanded plan (he ends up wintering there, not just spending a season).
  • **Dustin** — Learn Teaching from Henri (apprenticeship prerequisite).
  • **Wilhelm** — undecided between Ireland weather-magic fieldwork and a research track reverse-engineering formulaic (ritual) magic's underlying structure by close study of Hermetic ritual, spontaneous, potion, and enchantment sub-systems plus the semi-integrated longevity-ritual and Parma Magica traditions — looking for the shared principle underneath all of it.
  • **Éogan** — developing spells to industrialize dried-fruit and fruit-juice separation as a **non-magical, tradable commodity** for dockside trade, with an eye toward tribunal-to-tribunal arbitrage (some tribunals police magically-produced goods far more strictly than others).
  • **Dustin** — two seasons teaching his apprentice **Stijntje** a minor virtue: **Inventive Genius** in spring, then **Auram** in summer.
  • **Dietrich** — a season getting initiated (through one of the tribunal contacts made this week) into a minor virtue, so he can formally teach the folk-magic system at his Cologne cathedral school starting Fall — needed to satisfy his twice-yearly teaching obligation as a master there.
  • **Summer Fog** vis-source season: confirmed assigned to **Valerian**. Still unassigned: the **Black Horse of Boulogne** vis-source season.
**Running gag.** Wilhelm's graduation research project turns out to be a large stone dish that is **always full of grain** — **six million cubic yards'** worth before it would ever run dry, a delay-cast effect that delays by *volume poured out* rather than by time, a standard Hermetic ritual effect, not a homebrew "virtual" spell — magically produced content by any tribunal's reckoning, and thus a genuine arbitrage asset next to the covenant's existing enchanted freshwater barrels. He'd apparently had it out and in casual use for weeks before it occurred to him, entirely without irony, to mention it to his hosts.

title: Casting the annual Aegis of the Hearth near Harfleur
date: Fall 1223, as the fleet splits for the season
notes: Before scattering for the winter, the fleet convenes near Harfleur for the covenant's now-annual Aegis renewal. An exceptional roll makes the casting trivially safe. Two open snags: the Hound of Cassel isn't on the Master Chart and so isn't covered, and Ka'wa'ill — a magical creature himself — may need his own way past the boundary.
body_text:
Rather than let the covenant scatter for the season without magical protection, the fleet arranged to meet up near **Harfleur**, on the Channel, before splitting in different directions — a short detour, since Dagmar's ritual casting only takes a matter of minutes once everyone's in position.
**Target: the Master Chart**, aboard the Tide of Memory — the same enchanted item Dagmar inherited from Solving that tracks the fleet's ships. Casting the Aegis on the Chart extends its protection to every ship the Chart tracks, without needing each hull cast individually.
**Confirmed covered:** Veðrdreki (the Storm Dragon). **Confirmed NOT covered:** the **Hound of Cassel** — Wilhelm's newly assigned ship isn't on the Master Chart at all, so the Aegis doesn't reach it. ("I'm sure that won't come up," — Wilhelm, tempting fate.)
**The roll was absurd** — total around 30 against a routine casting threshold, high enough that the table joked Dagmar could've dropped ten points and still made it. Vis spent: 6 pawns, Rego and Vim in some combination.
**Tokens for outsiders:** per the ritual's design, participating magi can hand out minor-enchantment tokens that let a non-covenant person pass the Aegis' boundary safely — Éogan is assumed to have made one for **Wilhelm**, leaning on their existing Arcane Connection. **Open question:** Ka'wa'ill is a magical creature, and the Aegis is specifically built to keep those out — does he need a token too, and can one even be made for him?

**Stijntje** (apprentice's share) — 5 into **Code of Hermes**, 5 into **Animal Handling**, and enough into **Magic Theory** to round out the level she was already close to completing.

Éogan — 5 into Aquam (enough to reach the next level), 5 into mastering Mighty Torrent of Water (put toward quick-casting), 2 into Code of Hermes.

Dustin — 4 into Magic Theory, 4 into Creo, 4 into Terram.

Stijntje (apprentice's share) — 5 into Code of Hermes, 5 into Animal Handling, and enough into Magic Theory to round out the level she was already close to completing.

title: Overland to Carrick: a toll road, the Hill of Uisneach, and the road to Cruachan
notes: Dropped past Dublin by the Brineborn and Scholar's Wake — which then continue on to winter at the Isle of Man rather than the party itself — Éogan, Dustin, and Stijntje strike out overland for Carrick, by way of Tara, a talked-down toll stop, the Hill of Uisneach, and the threshold lands around Cruachan.
body_text:
The **Brineborn** and **Scholar's Wake** drop the party just past **Dublin**, then continue up the coast to **Drogheda** to spare them the walk before turning off to winter at the **Isle of Man** — the crews, not the travelers; the plan is to reconvene back in Dublin once the ice breaks in spring.
Heading inland toward the **Hill of Tara** — the seat of the Hibernian Tribunal's own meeting-place, ringed by burial mounds Éogan has seen before as an apprentice — the party is stopped by **three armed men** on the road, plausibly a toll, plausibly closer to banditry.
**Éogan talks them down entirely** — a Communication roll in Gaelic using his travel-jargon specialty, dropping into the local dialect convincingly enough that the toll-men immediately clock him as native to the area and wave the group through, half-apologizing for having pegged them as an easy foreign mark.
An Intelligence-based **Ireland/magical-sites** check (very strong roll) turns up the **Hill of Uisneach** just off the route — a site of old fire festivals and bird-flight divination, especially potent for reading the coming winter's severity when visited in the fall. The party detours to stop there.
Continuing deeper toward **Cruachan**, close to Samhain, the land shifts character — genuine threshold territory, "the monstrous, the uncanny, the underworld" close to the surface. Éogan tells Stijntje ghost-stories about **Fomorians** still lurking in the forests, partly to keep her steering clear of exactly the places that need steering clear of.
Cruachan itself isn't a proper Hermetic covenant — scattered **magical enclaves**, some temporary, some closer to permanent ritual-farming settlements. Hermetic magi are treaty-bound to **no more than three days at a time** inside Connacht itself, so the party keeps their stop brief before pushing on north to winter at **Carrick**.

title: Wintering at Carrick: a border fortress town, and an idiosyncratic Bonisagus
notes: Carrick turns out to be a strategic chokepoint disproportionately fortified for its size. Dustin spends the winter soaking up language and culture with Éogan translating; en route they pass a Bonisagus magus whose narrow, idiosyncratic focus on a handful of Arts baffles Dustin.
body_text:
**Carrick**, though a small town, sits at a geographic **bottleneck** along the northern valley route through Ireland — the natural corridor an English invasion would have to funnel through — and is built up militarily well beyond what its population would otherwise justify. Not because it defends anything valuable in itself, but because whoever holds it can stall an advance.
Interior Ireland reads less like a melting pot and more like a **salad bowl** — communities half a mile apart keeping fiercely distinct dialects, folklore, and even magical idiosyncrasies, without necessarily being hostile to their neighbors. On the way in, the party passes a **Bonisagus magus** who has narrowed his entire practice down to a handful of Arts and Techniques, to the flat exclusion of everything else — a decision that reads as arbitrary rather than tactical, and leaves Dustin quietly baffled.
**Dustin** spends his downtime soaking in language and culture (beyond his tutoring obligations); **Éogan** acts as willing translator and uses the time to get to know **Stijntje** better.

title: Caris's parting gift: Erroneous Meditations on the Enigma
notes: Caris warms up to Dagmar over the winter, eventually lending him a personal — and, per Caris, worthless — text. A strong Premonitions read reveals it as something else entirely: an extraordinarily detailed account, in diary form, of someone who vanished and came back. The parallel to Solving's own disappearance is not subtle.
body_text:
Dagmar spent much of the winter trying — and, for a long stretch, failing — to get Caris to engage socially at all; the Criamon magus ignored him outright for what felt like weeks before finally acknowledging him with a blunt "has the library been suitable for your work?"
Once engaged, Caris proved genuinely willing to talk shop, using an archer's metaphor for the Enigma: aim close and small errors don't matter, but aim at something near the horizon and the same small error becomes miles of drift — and some magi, having only ever aimed close, mistake confidence for precision.
Caris eventually lent Dagmar a personal text, dismissively titled **"Erroneous Meditations on the Enigma"** — his own tone throughout is some version of "I already told you it's worthless, but if it makes you stop asking, fine."
**Dagmar's Premonitions roll came back exceptional.** The text reads like a diary — someone trying to articulate an experience with the logical throughlines missing, the way a dream account never quite holds together. Whatever else it is, it's an **extremely high-resolution single data point** on someone who **disappeared and returned**, trying to describe what happened to them.
Unstated but obvious at the table: this is close kin to the covenant's own defining mystery — **Solving's disappearance into Twilight** in 1220, and the possibility he could still return the same way this account's author apparently did. Dagmar is very interested; this may become his next research thread.

title: Dagmar's Falcon's Cliff harvest
notes: Heading north from Oleron, Dagmar stops to harvest the newly claimed Falcon's Cliff vis source — a clean, well-executed capture with a strong yield.
body_text:
En route north from Oleron, Dagmar stops to work the newly claimed **Falcon's Cliff** vis source — timed to the falcon's annual clutch, where a serpent tries to steal the egg each year.
**Method:** an Intellego effect to pinpoint the nest and egg precisely, grogs stationed at range around the site, and **Eyes of the Eagle** to spot the serpent's approach and signal the grogs in time to intercept and capture it alive (uncertain at the time whether the vis-bearing material needed the creature dead or alive — it turned out either the egg or the captured snake could be converted afterward via a bit of magical working).
**Result: a clean success** — a strong "even/odd" roll came up favorably, yielding a hearty six weeks' worth of vis from the harvest.

title: The changeling boy: Rody
notes: Passing back through Cruachan, a hedge mage hands Éogan a young Gifted boy to deliver onward, as custom apparently allows. Days into the journey, Éogan works out the boy isn't human at all — and Stijntje independently starts to suspect the same. The party chooses discretion over confrontation, and a real missing child's fate is left to the receiving mages.
body_text:
On the way back through Cruachan, before Samhain-season traffic, a **hedge mage** approaches Éogan with a young boy in tow and asks outright whether he's a Hermetic magus. On confirming, the hedge mage hands the boy over with no more ceremony than "he's a little late, but he's owed delivery" to the Hermetic covenant near the Hill of Uisneach — and simply trusts that presenting a Hermetic magus with the boy counts as fulfilling the obligation, no receipt required. Éogan accepts him.
**The boy: "Rody," roughly eight and a half.** Talkative, unbothered, and matter-of-fact about his circumstances — his older brother was Gifted too, and was "eaten by goblins" before he could be handed over; Rody was collected a couple of months later as, presumably, the replacement delivery. He's more curious than distressed, and will happily talk anyone's ear off given the chance — including several increasingly creative insults about how badly **Dustin** smells, which read less like genuine complaint and more like Rody converting general unease into something he can weaponize.
Days into the return journey, **Éogan's Fairy Lore roll** (with his usual bonus to social rolls involving fae) catches something off in Rody's sleep — irregular breathing, joints bending the wrong way, an arm folded under him at an angle a human wouldn't hold. **Rody is a changeling.**
Éogan brings this to Dustin privately. Later the same day, unprompted, **Stijntje independently confronts Dustin**: "why are you so concerned about Rody... he's a creature, he's not a boy." Dustin deflects (a successful Communication/Leadership roll) without fully shutting her down — her curiosity is "latent," not resolved.
**The decision:** not force (too risky without an inescapable trap already laid — floated a salt circle as a fallback), not confrontation, not trade for now. The party completes the delivery as tasked, but plans to quietly brief the receiving Hermetic magi on their suspicion, reasoning this isn't their tribunal or their specialty to solve. **Open thread:** the actual Gifted child this changeling replaced is still out there somewhere with the Fae, and nobody the party trusts to find him has been told yet.

title: A hidden regio near Carnac
notes: Continuing his coastal survey between Fudarus and Confluensis territory, Dagmar's Eyes of the Eagle roll comes back an outrageous 52 and turns up a low-profile regio in sea caves near Carnac — apparently unnoticed by Carnac itself. He opts to explore it solo with grogs rather than loop the covenant in, expecting to be blamed for something regardless. Resolved: rowing in, Dagmar meets Tormente, a magnitude-10 dragon guarding the first layer, who sets him an errand (carry a jewelled Roman crown to its estranged kin near Scarborough) to earn passage deeper; the regio stays half-opened (t025).
body_text:
Continuing north from the Falcon's Cliff harvest, Dagmar resumes the **regio survey** he'd heard rumors about at the Tribunal, working the stretch of coast **between Fudarus and Confluensis** territory.
**Method:** Eyes of the Eagle (plus an aura bonus) to scan for the tell-tale visual distortion of a regio boundary at long range — deliberately steering wide of Carnac itself along the way, since Dagmar's been avoiding known covenants' territory generally.
**The roll: 52.** Far and away the highest number rolled at this table to date. The result: sea caves under the cliffs near Carnac, giving off a regio signature described as **a mirror-flash rather than a broadcast** — undetectable at normal range, and seemingly unnoticed by Carnac itself, whose own local aura reads as unremarkable. Getting inside means rowing into the caves.
**Decision:** rather than loop Carnac in and risk a diplomatic mess ("I'll just cut to the chase of them blaming us for something"), Dagmar takes a handful of grogs and explores by rowboat alone. **To be continued** — the GM flagged this as something to develop further before the next session.
**Into the regio: the dragon Tormente.**
Dagmar rows into the **Carnac sea-cave** with three grogs — **Angus** (helmsman, pirate, and reliable if boastful storyteller), **Foxglove** (scout, rogue, and acquirer of useful objects), and **Peter** — his **Eyes of the Eagle** and **Clear Sight of the Naiad** still up (the spells that found the place; he can see through water, fog, and dark).
**Probing in.** He casts a spontaneous **Intēllego Mentem** "is anyone around" — modelled on the smell-silver spell, reading minds like a sense, stronger signal meaning nearer — and picks up the faint edges of the **Carnac covenant**, a small **parasitic village** beside it, one or two people on the shore, and, deeper in, **one signal unlike anything he has ever felt before**. A quick tarot draw (Knight of Cups reversed, Eight of Wands reversed) foreshadows what's coming. **Piercing the Magical Veil** confirms a clear **onion-layer** structure — and that the strange thing ahead is *barring the way forward*.
**Crossing the first threshold**, Dagmar's over-tuned vision catches cobalt-blue flashes off what looks like **dozens of little mirrors** — then the wall *shudders and exhales*. The mirrors are **scales**. It is a **dragon**, slumped into the water and rising above it, filling the passage — roughly 45 feet of visible flank, 25 feet high, a leg going deep into the water. Only **Foxglove** glimpses its head lift and turn; to the others it stays a wall of scales. Magical Lore reads its resistance in the **50s — a magnitude-10 creature** — and the regio, oddly, as **more attuned to Auram than Aquam** despite all the water. Dagmar's read: this is a **guardian**, posted to protect an otherwise-defensible threshold; the way deeper is unobstructed *except* for the dragon in it.
**The parley.** Speaking mind-to-mind in Latin (**Posing the Silent Question**, **Words of the Unbroken Silence**), Dagmar rouses it. The dragon — **Tormente** — asks whether he serves **"Jeffrey the First,"** a long-dead king of Brittany whose *"quest of learning"* it seems to guard; Dagmar (House Criamon, Covenant of Sjórseiðr — all names Tormente has never heard) disclaims any royal commission and professes to seek knowledge for its own sake. Pressed for a **great deed or a quest**, Dagmar boasts of the covenant's Tribunal victory — champion of the magical contests of all Normandy — and demonstrates his Intēllego on request, penetrating with a burst of confidence.
**The price.** Satisfied, Tormente raises an arm from the water and deposits on the boat a **heavy jewelled golden crown**, Roman in style, dazzling and far too heavy to wear long. It is an **offering of peace** for Tormente's **estranged kin** — a dragon that *"will not speak to me"* — dwelling in a **sea-cliff cave above the waves off the English northeast coast, near Scarborough / Newcastle, just short of Scotland.** Carry the crown to the kin and reconcile them, and Tormente will **deem Dagmar worthy of passing deeper** into the regio. Dagmar accepts, and gives orders to head **north** to find the kin — possibly by way of **Stonehenge**, to collect Llewellyn and finally cash in the time-crystal (t018, t066). The Carnac regio itself stays only half-opened (t025).

title: The Tribunal prize draft — Sjórseiðr's full slate

Spend rule: a vis source costs its annual pawn-yield; a library book costs 3 (summa) or 2 (tractatus/lab text). Full 31 spent — all four vis sources, then all seven library picks.
body_text:
As the 1st-place covenant (the **"Siege of Normandy"**), Sjórseiðr won **31 prize pawns** and drafted first; Dagmar led the picks on the covenant's behalf, resolved asynchronously with the GM after the session. Spend rule: a vis source costs its annual pawn-yield; a library book costs a flat 3 (summa) or 2 (tractatus / lab text).
**Vis sources claimed (4) — 12 pawns:**
• **Mont-Saint-Michel Tide Pools** — Aquam, 5 pawns/yr *(5)* — the top-value coastal source, taken with the 1st-overall pick.
• **The Falcon's Cliff** — Animal, annual *(2)* — a falcon's-nest cliff; foil the serpent's egg-theft for Animal vis, catch the snake for Vim.
• **The Diedne Garden** — Herbam, 3 pawns/yr *(3)*.
• **Norman Barrow Frost** — Corpus, 2 pawns/yr *(2)*.
**Library picks (7) — 19 pawns:**
• **De Lapii** — Terram summa (L17 · Q14), branch-specific *(3)* — the crown jewel; Éogan's clear top priority.
• **Subtle Knives** — Penetration summa *(3)* — Éogan's "far second."
• **The Babble Within Thought** — Mentem summa (L12 · Q11) *(3)* — a Criamon-relevant text for Dagmar.
• **The Compact Explained** — Order of Hermes Lore tractatus *(2)*.
• **Insights from Twilight** — Magic Theory summa (L6) *(3)* — lifts every magus's lab work and feeds Wilhelm's & Dustin's research.
• **Legends of Brittany** — Faerie Lore summa (L3) *(3)* — real utility given Rán, Ka'wa'ill, and the covenant's fae dealings.
• **Research Notes on Aegis of the Hearth** — Spell Mastery tractatus *(2)* — improves the covenant's annual Aegis.
**Total: 12 + 19 = 31 of 31 prize pawns spent.**

title: The augury lesson: the art is choosing the signal
notes: Detailing the Hill of Uisneach stop from the Overland to Carrick leg: Wilhelm gets his first concrete field-insight for the folk-magic thesis — the load-bearing skill in local bird-flight augury is not the spell but the reading.
body_text:
At the **Hill of Uisneach** — the old fire-festival and bird-flight divination site the party detoured to on the overland road — Wilhelm and Éogan arrive just after a **divination ritual** has wrapped. Cleaning up after it is a roughly **twelve-year-old apprentice** to one of the local hedge-magi, doing busy-work but willing to describe, imperfectly, what the rite involved.
Wilhelm reads the process with **Magic Theory** (his strong suit — a comfortable, non-stress success) and comes away underwhelmed by the *spell* and fascinated by everything around it. The working itself is mechanical and straightforward. The true art of the **auguri** is in **choosing the correct signal**: the birds are doing fifteen things fifteen times, three of which might answer the question asked *this* time, three others another time, one just there for its own sake and never yet pulled out. Selecting *which* reading, and *when* it is auspicious to ask, is at least as load-bearing as the incantation.
Wilhelm clocks the shape of what he's after: this is magic that **leans on the inherent power of the environment** — the full moon, the turn to autumn, the land underfoot — rather than on the individual sorcerer. Where **Hermetic theory strips the context out** for a formulaic effect that works anywhere and anytime, this tradition insists the environment and the time of year *matter* — and that, to Wilhelm, is the point: *if I can make this subset of magic easier by leaning on something else, fantastic.*
He spends the following days probing people they meet and taking notes, folding the augury insight toward his thesis (see t009) and the folk-magic system he means to formalize (t019). His scribe not being present, he keeps his own record.

title: Small gods on the shoulder: the fae that follow Éogan and Stijntje
notes: Only Wilhelm's Awareness catches it: small fae keep gathering on Éogan and Stijntje as the party nears Connacht. The locals treat it as nothing; Wilhelm, tactful, says nothing either.
body_text:
As the party moves deeper toward **Connacht** around Samhain, an Awareness check goes round the table. Éogan (a near-miss) and Stijntje are **completely unaware**; only **Wilhelm** notices — and what he notices is that the two of them keep collecting **small fae** the way some people attract butterflies.
A little **brownie** riding a shoulder, gone the instant he looks straight at it. A **pixie-light** settling on Éogan's head and winking out. A gnome half-clambering out of a backpack. The first few times Wilhelm assumes he's seeing things; after half a dozen sightings in different contexts — the creatures behaving as if this is entirely normal, everyone else simply *ignoring* them — he realizes it isn't him.
The GM's read: **Éogan** draws them by virtue of a Connacht upbringing that respected the land where it **bleeds in and out of faerie regiones**; **Stijntje** by simple virtue of still being a child. To the locals, the presence of these **small gods** is unremarkable — you leave a bowl of milk out at night and get on with it.
Wilhelm, who has done enough fieldwork to know that pointing such things out tends to give offense, keeps it to himself and files it away. Éogan, for his part, assumes any odd behavior of Wilhelm's is just a foreigner reacting to ordinary warding customs. **New character note:** small fae are demonstrably drawn to Éogan and Stijntje (see t068).

title: Brussel the púca asks to be taught
notes: A talking black horse — a púca — hails Wilhelm in Latin to be taught folk magic, and parts with a rowan-wood horseshoe. Wilhelm's first genuinely eager student in the wild.
body_text:
On the spring road back east — "past the edge of the world," as Éogan puts it — the party pauses at a stream, and Wilhelm hears a voice in **Latin** from twenty paces off: *are you the one teaching magic to all?* Without looking he says yes, then turns to find a **black horse** addressing him.
Éogan, via **Ireland / Fairy Lore**, identifies it: a **púca** — a trickster fae given to inconveniencing travelers greatly but rarely to lasting harm, and *not* the kind that steals children or spoils milk. It gives its use-name as **Brussel** (Wilhelm notes, correctly, that a wizard's by-name is at best a **weak Arcane Connection**, not the true name).
Wilhelm teaches it the folk basics — a **circle** to bind and protect energies — and the horse traces one with a hoof, imperfectly but earnestly (*"you might make it slightly better by dragging your hoof in one continuous line"*). Brussel offers to let Wilhelm **ride it** in exchange for instruction; Wilhelm declines with great courtesy — he is an unskilled rider and gets violently seasick on anything that moves, and *"would not be a good teacher if I were vomiting on your head every twenty steps."* Brussel, it transpires, is no fonder of being ridden either.
At parting the delighted púca gifts Wilhelm a **horseshoe of rowan wood**. Wilhelm accepts it as a treasured gift and files it in the **covenant treasury** — moved that Brussel is the **first entity outside his own research staff** to take real interest in his work and agree to be taught. First wild student of the folk system; see t069.

title: The assistants return: the madness cost, and the brass acorn
notes: Auto-drafted from the 2026-08-08 session transcript; not yet owner-reviewed.
body_text:
On the return road after leaving Carrick, Wilhelm's two research assistants intercept the party — Carl hale, Isaac on a crutch and healing from a beating. Their report: they taught Wilhelm's folk techniques to twelve-to-fifteen people, and the method worked — but for a minority it pushed the mind past breaking. One student killed themselves; another killed two others. The local lord, down several field-hands, had the pair beaten and thrown out (not charged with murder, but no longer welcome). Reviewing their competent notes, Wilhelm judges it no defect in the teaching: the madness is a cost of the magic itself.

The assistants also carry stranger news. A hedge mage they encountered claims to have travelled through time, and said Wilhelm should find a brass acorn in his luggage — a memento “from a previous future visit.” Wilhelm finds it, exactly so. A later Intēllego Vim check turns up no magical residue at all, ruling out a teleported plant and leaving the temporal claim unexplained.

title: A ward drawn around Rody
notes: Continues 'The changeling boy: Rody.' Wilhelm is brought in on the changeling, and his casual folk-ward demonstration doubles as a test — will Rody be able to cross a Ward against Faeries?
body_text:
With the changeling confirmed, Éogan and Dustin **bring Wilhelm in** — partly because none of them has magic that could actually *hold* a fae, and Wilhelm's folk wards handle only low-magnitude sprites and brownies, nothing strong enough to be wearing a Gifted boy's shape convincingly.
Over a day of the march east (Rody having a little rudimentary Latin, and Wilhelm practicing his teaching), Wilhelm uses the boy as a live audience for the folk basics, then **demonstrates a set of protective wards** drawn as circles: a **ward against the spirits of the land**, a **ward against the infernal**, and — casually, drawing it around the group as he casts — a **ward against fairies**. He steps out of the fairy-ward ring himself and then invites Rody across, to see whether the boy can pass it.
**The mechanics, as the GM laid them out:** a folk **Ward against Faeries** at roughly **base level 10** — inefficient the way ward magic always is, in that it only binds a creature it can "get through," i.e. one of low enough Might. It is *highly unlikely* to hold a changeling powerful enough to counterfeit a Gifted child, but the test costs nothing and might reveal something. Wilhelm's cast lands well over the level.
**The test:** whether **Rody steps out of the circle**. Either way, the party still means to complete the delivery east — toward the **Hill of Tara**, where they'll rendezvous with Wilhelm's returning research assistants and hand the boy on to the receiving Hermetic magi — and to brief those magi on the deception. The real Gifted child Rody replaced is still out there (t023, q026).

title: Foxglove robs the dragon
notes: A covenant grog quietly robs Tormente's hoard the same night — while Dagmar is trying to stay in the dragon's good graces to earn passage deeper. Consequence seed.
body_text:
Back at the ship, **Angus** gathers the sixteen crew and spins a **broadly honest** account of the dragon for a night of bought drinks (*"the creepy wizard made us go, he spoke spells at it, and it gave us treasure"*) — **Peter** adding embellishments that aren't quite true, **Foxglove** conspicuously **downplaying the treasure**.
Because Foxglove — avaricious to the marrow — has other plans. That night she quietly takes the rowboat **back into the cave alone**, anchors it, and dives the twenty-odd feet to the cave floor, where **gold and trinkets have spilled forward** from the hoard. She gathers all she can carry, smuggles roughly **five bags of it** aboard, and hides it for herself, brushing past **Peter** with a caught-red-handed lie about running a late errand for Dagmar (a clean Guile success). Examined later, the coin is mostly **Roman** in style — priceless, and useless as currency; she means to keep every piece.
**The wrinkle:** this is an **unsanctioned theft from Tormente's hoard**, committed the very night Dagmar has agreed to run the dragon's errand and is depending on its goodwill to pass deeper into the regio. Neither Dagmar nor the dragon knows yet (c026).

title: Dagmar's next leg: north to England, and messages by Redcap
notes: Dagmar's stated forward plan following 'Foxglove robs the dragon': the next leg heads north to England (a town within the Stonehenge Tribunal), sending Redcap messages to Llewellyn ex Miscellanea (a regio-exploration invite, ~X weeks out per the captain's estimate) and to Paulus ex Merinita (ward status). Deliberately NOT sent from near Carnac. Map/GM seed: the Tide of Memory leaves Carnac northbound up the English coast toward a second dragon, watching for regios and taking easy trade only incidentally.
body_text:
Dagmar's plan for the next leg, set after the Carnac regio.

**North to England, and word ahead by Redcap.** Having knocked on the regio's door — and found a **dragon** behind it — Dagmar means to head **north to England**. He will put in at a town within the bounds of the **Stonehenge Tribunal** and commission the **Redcaps** to carry two messages:

- To **Llewellyn ex Miscellanea**: that Dagmar will be passing back through in **X weeks** (X set by the captain's estimate for the next leg), with an offer for Llewellyn to join him in exploring a regio.
- To **Paulus ex Merinita**: asking after the **ward** — how it comes along, and when it might be ready.

Notably, he will **not** send these messages from the vicinity of **Carnac**.

**Up the English coast, at speed.** With his mail away, Dagmar takes the **Tide of Memory** up the coast of England toward the **second dragon's** reported location. He keeps an eye out for regios along the way, and the ship may take on a little easy trade when it resupplies — but the Tide is making the passage with all speed, so neither the regio-watching nor the trading is likely to come to much.

title: The feast at Cruachan: Rody delivered, and the matching necklaces
notes: Auto-drafted from the 2026-08-08 session transcript; not yet owner-reviewed.
body_text:
The party reaches the covenant at Cruachan and briefs its magi before bringing the changeling inside. Gráinne and Tadhg — versed in Faerie magic — receive them warmly, hear that “Rody” is Fae and may lead to the real, taken child, and agree to help: come to a feast the next night after dusk, and bring Rody carrying a knotted-wood token so he can pass the Aegis.

At the feast, Tadhg has Rody swear a preliminary apprentice's oath. Dustin notices Rody and Stijntje wearing matching necklaces (“we made them for each other”) — faerie-associated but not magical objects — and, fearing Stijntje had been swapped too, checks; to his relief she has not. Rody is left in the covenant's keeping, their Fae specialists to hold and question him and, with luck, trace the child he replaced.

title: The Hound of Cassel and the three sealed chests
notes: Auto-drafted from the 2026-08-08 session transcript; not yet owner-reviewed.
body_text: Set up with the Hound of Cassel as his ship at the Isle of Man, Wilhelm searches her over — a plain merchantman, no lab — and turns up three small, magically-sealed boxes. They are spoils of Valdemar's raid on a Scarem Montem vessel: Normandy law let him take the non-magical cargo, but magical goods fall under the Code's bar on depriving a magus of magical power, so the boxes have sat in trust, meant for return and never returned — awkward now that Scarem Montem has walked out of the Tribunal in the schism. Their contents stay sealed. Wilhelm lays a month-long Vim ward on the hull, making the boat “technically magical,” as both deterrent and legal fig-leaf.
